items.text:
By Rose Muasya
A mention of peace often brings images of war, bloodshed, displaced families and communities torn apart by violence. But for Richie Olaka, peace begins long before the guns fall silent. It is reflected in whether children can attend school, families can put food on the table, people can access healthcare and communities can resolve their differences without resorting to violence.
Even access to water during drought, he argues, can determine whether communities coexist peacefully or compete over scarce resources.
“Peace is not just the absence of war. It is a situation where different elements of a community or society work together to ensure homeostasis,” says Olaka.
Olaka, a civil servant working in the Department for Refugee Services under the Ministry of Interior, likens a peaceful society to a functioning human body, where organs such as the lungs, liver, kidneys and heart work together to sustain life.
“We cannot have peace without development, and vice versa,” he says.
His understanding of peace has been shaped by years of public service, community engagement and professional training, including a Rotary Peace Fellowship at Makerere University in Uganda, which he completed in 2023.
The Rotary Peace Centres promote peace through academic training, practical experience and global networking, equipping professionals to become effective catalysts for peace. The fellowships focus on areas such as youth, conflict prevention and development, recognising that young people are both a driving force in national development and, in some circumstances, among those involved in violence, particularly during political movements.
Olaka’s interest in peacebuilding dates back to his university days in 2007, when Kenya was recovering from the violence that followed the disputed General Election.
As a student at Moi University, he witnessed the devastating effects of violence and joined other young people in peace initiatives. Together with police officers and humanitarian workers, he participated in peace walks in Eldoret, Kakamega and Nandi Hills, areas that had experienced ethnic clashes.
“The mayhem and bloodshed within communities was heart-rending,” Olaka said.
Although he had little formal knowledge of peacebuilding at the time, the experience taught him that peace could not be left to security officers, politicians or international organisations alone. Ordinary citizens also had a responsibility to rebuild relationships and restore trust.
Years later, the Rotary Peace Fellowship strengthened his understanding of how peace can be built and sustained. The programme brought together professionals from different backgrounds, including academia, security, finance, law and journalism.
“Traditionally, people believe a peace practitioner is someone working with the United Nations on peace missions. But peace work is not confined to a particular person or profession,” he says.
A teacher who consistently shows up to teach, a public officer who treats people fairly or a community member who helps resolve disagreements can all contribute to peace.
“Peacebuilding is not only about going to a peacekeeping mission and doing what officers on deployment are doing,” observes the peace fellow.
The one-year fellowship combined academic learning with field experiences and a practical social change initiative. In Rwanda, Olaka examined efforts to rebuild the country following the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. He also engaged with institutions and communities in Uganda, exploring governance, displacement and the relationship between environmental pressures and conflict.
The experiences reinforced his belief that lasting peace requires more than security interventions. It also depends on strong institutions, responsible management of resources and opportunities for people to participate in decisions affecting their lives.
As part of his practical initiative in Kenya, Olaka worked with national government administration officers to promote positive peace, drawing on his experience in public administration.
His exposure to displacement during the fellowship also deepened his interest in refugee affairs. After returning to Kenya, he was transferred to the Department of Refugee Services, where he now works on livelihoods.
Kenya hosts about 900,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, many of them in Kakuma and Dadaab.
“Supporting displaced people is not simply a humanitarian obligation but part of building peaceful communities,” Olaka notes.
The peace expert argues that peace must be considered from the perspectives of both refugees and their host communities. Where people lack opportunities, struggle to access essential services or feel excluded, tensions can deepen and potentially lead to violence.
Olaka’s work on refugee livelihoods seeks to create an environment in which refugees can pursue opportunities and build their lives with dignity.
“I define peace as dignity. Whether it is the host community or the refugee community, if people are not living in peace, we cannot say that the community is peaceful,” he says.
Recently, he has participated in visits to refugee-led organisations and food donation initiatives alongside humanitarian groups, including Rotary, as part of efforts to give back to society. Such engagements, he hopes, will encourage more people to see peacebuilding as a shared responsibility.
He also advocates using existing community networks, including churches, mosques and chamas, to promote dialogue and peaceful coexistence.
“How do we activate peace?” he poses. “It is about taking advantage of structures that already exist and leveraging the mechanisms within our communities,” he adds.
Such networks can bring people together to discuss differences and identify common ground, even when they disagree on politics, religion or other issues.

items.text:
South Korea's top court overturns jail term for former PM Han
November 19, 2026
The South Korean Supreme Court on Thursday overturned a 15-year prison sentence for the country's former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo for playing a key role in the 2024 imposition of martial law by ex-President Yoon Suk Yeol.
The case will now return to a lower court, the Seoul High Court, which had sentenced Han to 15 years in prison in May.
Why was South Korean ex-PM Han's sentence overturned?
Han was convicted for helping plan the insurrection by suggesting that Yoon hold a Cabinet meeting to make martial law seem legitimate.
He also allegedly tried to collect Cabinet members' signatures on a related document and reviewed orders to cut off power and water to media outlets critical of Yoon.
The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled that prosecutors had not sufficiently proven the case and ordered a review of the conviction.
At the same time, the top court upheld a four-year prison term for Yoon's wife, Kim Keon Hee, on charges of corruption, including manipulating stock prices and bribery.
What was the 2024 insurrection?
On December 3, 2024, former president Yoon Suk Yeol abruptly declared martial law, prompting massive protests and a showdown in parliament.
At the time, Yoon said the declaration was needed to rid the country of "pro-North Korean forces" and followed it by sending troops and police into parliament.
But enough lawmakers managed to enter the assembly chamber to unanimously vote down Yoon's decree, forcing his cabinet to rescind it.
Yoon was impeached and later found guitly of leading an insurrection and sentenced to life in prison.

items.text:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino is officially facing two election opponents trying to end his 11 years in office.
Philippe Diallo of France and Kohzo Tashima of Japan met the midnight deadline in Zurich to file entry papers with nomination letters from five member federations, FIFA confirmed on Thursday.
The vote by FIFA's 211 member federations will be held on March 18 in Rabat, Morocco.
Infantino's critics, led by UEFA, have been trying to replace him since his secretive plan to sell stakes in World Cup profits to private investors was revealed in July. He dropped the project amid a fierce backlash.
"(T)he candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidate," FIFA said in a statement.
FIFA has set a Feb. 18 deadline for its three-member election panel to tell the 211 members which candidates are approved to go on the ballot paper.
Candidates must pass an eligibility and integrity check by the panel, whose rulings can later be challenged at the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne, Switzerland.
Infantino also received heavy critism for FIFA's handling of the red card shown to United States striker Folarin Balogun during last summer's World Cup which resulted in his ban being overturned after an intervention by U.S. President Donald Trump.
Former Liverpool manager Jürgen Klopp has said he thinks Infantino should be replaced as FIFA president.
"There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense," Klopp, now the Germany head coach, said this week.
"I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse -- but here we are."
Who is Philippe Diallo?
The French Football Federation president, who played in Nantes' academy, has worked in football since 1992 and was a judge in FIFA's dispute resolution chamber for more than 20 years.
He said he has received "strong signs of support from other continents" when launching his bid for the FIFA presidency in Paris on Tuesday.
Diallo said the first figure from UEFA to push him to mount a challenge to Infantino was English FA chair Debbie Hewitt.
The 63-year-old has said he will try to convince his presidency rival Tashima to "join forces," but did not detail exactly what that might mean for their respective candidacies as they try to oust Infantino.
Who is Kohzo Tashima?
Tashima, 68, is the first person from Japan to run for FIFA presidency.
"It's not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built," he was quoted as saying by Reuters as he announced his intention to run for FIFA president.
"What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world."
He has been on FIFA's ruling committee since 2015 when Sepp Blatter was president.
Previously, Tashima was a footballer for Japan and head of his nation's federation. As a player, he earned seven Japans caps in 1979-80.
Associated Press contributed to this story.

items.text:
WASHINGTON -- North Carolina Courage forward Ashley Sanchez was named the 2026 NWSL Most Valuable Player on Wednesday after scoring a record-tying 20 goals this season.
"Coming back from some tough years, to have something like this, it's just incredible," Sanchez told reporters outside the at Lisner Auditorium on the campus of George Washington University, where the NWSL Awards Show was held. "And I think, for me, this year I've just proved to myself what I'm capable of. I think I was just really consistent, and that's something that I've always wanted out of my play, and I accomplished that."
Sanchez's 20 goals tied the NWSL record set in 2024 by Kansas City Current forward Temwa Chawinga, who also won the MVP and Golden Boot award that year. Sanchez also had five assists and led the NWSL with 25 goal contributions. Her 20 goals this season were more than her first five NWSL seasons combined.
She was traded to the North Carolina Courage from the Washington Spirit in January 2024 in a trade that she said at the time took her by surprise.
Sanchez also had a difficult 2023 World Cup, when she made the United States' roster and appeared to be in line for a prominent role, but did not play a single minute. She held back tears as she discussed her journey on Wednesday.
"I always felt confident in what I could do, but I knew that I had some things to work through to get here," Sanchez said. "And it was just all part of the journey, and I knew that was what was going to happen. It was kind of on me to figure out how to navigate myself out of that."
Sanchez has been a phenom since her early teenage years. In 2016, she became the first American player to compete at a U17 World Cup and a U20 World Cup in the same year. She is only the second player in the NWSL's 13-season history to win MVP on a team that failed to make the playoffs.
Chawinga, Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman, Denver Summit defender Janine Sonis and Portland Thorns FC forward Sophia Wilson were also finalists for the MVP award. Rodman and Chawinga will face off in Saturday's NWSL Championship across the city at Audi Field.
The Kansas City Current's Croix Bethune won the Midfielder of the Year award for the second time in three years. Her 11 assists set a new single-season NWSL record. Sonis was named the Defender of the Year after scoring 12 goals and adding eight assists from the fullback position for Denver Summit FC.
Gotham FC's Ann-Katrin Berger won the Goalkeeper of the Year award after recording 11 shutouts, second most in the league.
Jimmy Coenraets was named the NWSL Coach of the Year after leading the Utah Royals to their first playoff appearance. The Royals defeated the San Diego Wave FC in their first franchise playoff game to advance to the semifinals, where they lost to the Washington Spirit.
Gotham FC forward Jordynn Dudley was named the Rookie of the Year, marking the third time in four years that a Gotham player has won the honor.
Angel City FC defender Savy King won the Lauren Holiday Impact award for establishing Savy King of Hearts, a nonprofit focused on CPR awareness, preventive screenings, and heart health advocacy. King started the foundation after her own on-field cardiac emergency during a match in 2025, when she received life-saving intervention from medical staff and athletic trainers. Doctors discovered a heart abnormality after she was brought to the hospital.

items.text:
North Korea expanding uranium enrichment facility, UN nuclear watchdog says
North Korea can produce both highly enriched uranium and weapons-grade plutonium at its facilities, according to the IAEA.
North Korea is expanding a nuclear facility for enriching uranium, according to the head of the United Nations nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
An existing facility at the Yongbyon nuclear centre has been further expanded in the last couple of months, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday.
This comes as US President Donald Trump expressed his eagerness to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un while he is in Asia for an APEC leaders’ summit in China.
“Since mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by late October 2026,” Grossi said in a statement to the IAEA’s board of governors.
“The ongoing expansion of the DPRK’s uranium enrichment program remains extremely worrying,” he added, using North Korea’s official name, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.
Pyongyang has not allowed IAEA inspectors into the country for years. The IAEA, nevertheless, keeps watch on North Korea’s nuclear facilities, including through satellite imagery and open-source information.
North Korea has called its Yongbyon complex “the heart” of its nuclear programme. Nuclear weapons can be built using either highly enriched uranium or weapons-grade plutonium, and North Korea has facilities to produce both at Yongbyon.
North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui last week stressed that possessing such weapons was “the strongest guarantee” of his country’s sovereignty. Choe rejected the recent demand for North Korea’s complete nuclear disarmament by the Group of Seven (G7) economically powerful democracies.
Disarmament of the global nuclear weapons arsenal is likely to be a topic at the trilateral meeting between Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in Shenzhen, at Trump’s request.
While Trump expressed interest in meeting with Kim, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio later said no meeting was yet scheduled with the North Korean leader during Trump’s Asia visit. However, he added that the president is prepared to begin a new dialogue with Pyongyang.

items.text:
Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
November 19, 2026
As Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, Washington wants to tighten its blockade of Iran, but China remains Tehran's main oil buyer and Russia offers it political and logistical support.
And when Trump, Xi and Putin sit down together, Iran will not be at the table, even though Washington's pressure campaign against Tehran is expected to be among the issues discussed.
For Tehran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic. That relationship looks more complicated from Beijing and Moscow.
Both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran. But both have broader interests in their relationships with the United States and may see Iran partly through the prism of their own negotiations with Washington.
That raises a central question: Can Trump's strategy of economically isolating Iran succeed if China and Russia refuse to fully cooperate?
China is now Iran's economic lifeline
China is currently the most important destination for Iranian oil.
In 2025, it was widely reported that Chinese buyers took more than 80% of Iran's seaborne crude exports, much of it through independent refiners and at steep discount because of sanctions.
And as China provided Tehran an economic lifeline, Iran also became increasingly dependent on Chinese manufactured goods, machinery and industrial inputs.
Mohsen Solhdoost, an assistant professor of international relations at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, says China is important to Washington's strategy but not decisive on its own.
"If the objective is to reduce Iranian export earnings, restrict access to equipment and make economic and military recovery more difficult, the United States can achieve substantial results without Chinese cooperation," he told DW.
But forcing Iran to accept Washington's preferred nuclear or regional policies is another matter.
"The ability to interrupt trade is much easier to demonstrate than the ability to determine another government's political choices," Solhdoost said.
Sanctions enforcement raises pressure on Iran
That distinction has become more important as US sanctions enforcement and maritime blockade efforts have increased pressure on Iranian crude oil exports.
In November, Washington announced Task Force Iron Gate, an initiative aimed at disrupting the movement of sanctioned goods, military equipment and revenue through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.
Even so, these trade links have not disappeared. The commercial and security interests of countries including Iraq, Pakistan and Turkey mean that goods continue to move across the region, albeit under greater scrutiny.
As a result, China's role in Iran's economy remains significant, but Solhdoost argues that demand alone cannot sustain Iranian exports. The oil must be able to reach international markets.
"A Chinese buyer cannot keep Iranian export revenues flowing simply by remaining willing to buy if newly loaded tankers cannot reach the market," Solhdoost said.
Iran prepares for the worst
This economic pressure is shaping Tehran's financial planning.
A senior official at Iran's Plan and Budget Organization recently said the government was preparing its 2027-2028 budget under several scenarios, including one in which oil revenue falls to zero.
That does not mean Iran has adopted a zero-oil budget, but considering such a scenario illustrates how seriously Tehran views the situation.
At the same time, Chinese trade can preserve critical parts of the Iranian economy even if overall commerce shrinks.
Machinery, electronics, spare parts and industrial components can still reach Iran by rail and road. Such trade cannot replace maritime commerce at comparable scale or cost, but it can keep selected factories and infrastructure operating.
What does Beijing want?
Such Chinese support could help Iran endure pressure without preventing economic deterioration, says Solhdoost.
But even for Beijing supporting Iran economically does not mean supporting every Iranian policy.
A prolonged conflict around the Strait of Hormuz threatens wider energy supplies and global shipping. China therefore benefits from continued access to Iranian oil but also from regional stability.
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has maintained support for cooperation with Tehran while calling for negotiations, safe passage through Hormuz and stable energy supplies.
Russia can help, but how much?
Russia creates another obstacle to Iran's isolation. The two countries share access to the Caspian Sea and have expanded military, transport and economic cooperation.
Iranian officials have discussed ways of using Russian and northern trade routes to reduce the impact of American restrictions. There has also been speculation about oil swaps and deeper Russian assistance, although these claims remain difficult to verify.
Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East, believes the summit should be viewed within a larger attempt to manage the wars in both Ukraine and the Middle East.
"Russia, China and the United States appear to be seeking constructive dialogue and results that could shape a new security architecture in the international system," Vakhshiteh told DW.
The summit could be significant if it establishes a continuing format for dialogue rather than producing symbolic statements, Vakhshiteh says, while cautioning against expecting a dramatic settlement from a single meeting.

Solhdoost also warns against overstating Russian support for Iran.

items.summary:
Kenya’s marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir gets three-year ban for doping
Jepchirchir admitted to breaching anti-doping rules relating to the presence of banned substance EPO, Athletics Integrity Unit says.
Kenya’s reigning world and former Olympic marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been suspe
items.text:
Kenya’s marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir gets three-year ban for doping
Jepchirchir admitted to breaching anti-doping rules relating to the presence of banned substance EPO, Athletics Integrity Unit says.
Kenya’s reigning world and former Olympic marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been suspended for three years after testing positive for the banned substance EPO, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said.
Jepchirchir admitted to breaching anti-doping rules relating to the presence of a prohibited substance or its metabolites and to the use or attempted use of a prohibited substance or prohibited method, the AIU said in a statement on Thursday.
EPO, a synthetic form of erythropoietin, is a laboratory-made version of a natural hormone produced mainly by the kidneys that signals the bone marrow to make more red blood cells, according to the Mayo Clinic.
Athletes sometimes misuse synthetic EPO as a performance-enhancing drug to boost oxygen delivery to muscles and improve endurance.
Jepchirchir was provisionally suspended last month after the AIU, which investigates doping in track and field athletes on behalf of the sport’s governing body, World Athletics, returned an adverse analytical finding for EPO from an out-of-competition sample collected in Kenya before her Sydney Marathon victory in late August.
Jepchirchir has accepted the disqualification of all of her competitive results since July 17.
The 33-year-old won women’s marathon gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and the world title last year. She is also a former world record holder in the half marathon.
The Sydney Marathon, which noted that Jepchirchir’s in-competition test had returned negative, said Irine Cheptai is set to be elevated to 2026 women’s champion.
The AIU said it also sanctioned two other high-profile Kenyan runners.
Veronica Loleo, a half-marathon silver medallist at the 2026 world road running championships, was banned for three years after testing positive for EPO in an out-of-competition test.
Meanwhile, Ronald Korir, who placed fourth in the 2023 Berlin Marathon, received a six-year ban after abnormalities were found in his athlete biological passport, which he failed to explain. The AIU analysed 20 blood samples taken from Korir from May 6, 2023, to August 18, 2025, and identified abnormalities.
“The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go,” AIU chief executive Brett Clothier said in a statement.
“The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country.”
These were the latest in a long series of doping cases involving distance runners from Kenya.
Women’s marathon world record holder Ruth Chepng’etich, also from Kenya, was banned for three years in 2025 after admitting a charge related to a positive test for a banned diuretic. Former New York Marathon winner Albert Korir was given a five-year ban in March.

The 48 complainants accuse the government of violating Uganda's constitut
items.text:
Uganda deadly landslide survivors seek justice at the UN
- Published
Survivors of a 2019 landslide in eastern Uganda that killed more than 50 people have taken their fight for relocation and compensation to the United Nations.
The 48 complainants accuse the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to put effective disaster management measures in Bududa, a mountainous district prone to landslides.
Their case comes as heavy rains raise the risk of further landslides. They say the government relocation programme ignores their safety, land rights and livelihoods.
The UN Human Rights Committee is considering what is believed to be the first case seeking climate adaptation measures, one that could set a global precedent.
The landslide struck Bududa in 2019, killing more than 53 people, including 33 children. Years later, survivors say every spell of heavy rain brings back fears of another tragedy.
William Tsama, one of the claimants, lost four members of his family members.
"My quest should be a lesson," he said.
"Victims in such situations, ignored by governments, can take them to court to compel them to help their citizens."
The threat extends beyond landslides. The complainants say changing rainfall patterns and declining soil fertility have also affected farming, leaving many families struggling to secure their livelihoods.
"I want to get a new good place for my people, so even if I die, they will be okay. I am an old man, but I am doing it for my children," Tsama said.
The survivors first launched legal action in 2020 in Uganda, and received support from Ugandan environmental organisation Greenwatch three years later.
They are seeking compensation for lost family members and livelihoods, as well as emergency measures, including accessible early-warning systems in high-risk areas.
Greenwatch Executive Director Samantha Atukunda Kakuru Mwesigwa said the case is about changing how governments prepare and respond to climate-related disasters.
"Justice for claimants is not just about winning in court. It is about forcing government policy to keep pace with a changing climate, and ensuring loss and damage is no longer an afterthought in disaster management," she said.
The threat of climate-related disasters extends across East Africa.
In Kenya, floods and landslides killed at least 181 people between March and May 2024, according to the Kenya Red Cross. In Rwanda, floods and landslides killed 135 people in May 2023.
The dangers are also being felt further afield. In October 2026, a flash flood swept through Nepal's Gorkha district after a landslide blocked a river, washing away homes and infrastructure, and killing over 1,500 people.
"Disasters like the one in Bududa are only getting worse because of climate change – and they are happening all around the world, as we've seen recently and tragically in Nepal," ClientEarth lawyer Vesselina Newman said.
She said poorer countries, which have contributed relatively little to global emissions, are bearing some of the heaviest consequences of climate change and need greater financial support.
"High income countries must provide financial assistance and ensure that sufficient money goes directly to countries like Uganda, so they can roll out life-saving adaptation measures," she said.
Uganda introduced a resettlement plan for landslide-prone areas in 2011, but progress has been limited, with relatively few people relocated.
The government has now given residents of designated high-risk areas two months, from November to December, to leave or face forced eviction.
But the complainants say relocation must involve more than move people out of danger.
They want the government to protect their livelihoods, respect their land rights, and take account of individual needs.
The case is now before the United Nations Human Rights Committee, which will ask the Ugandan government to respond within six months.

items.title: Hippo kills 16-year-old student bathing at Lake Victoria in Homa Bay
items.summary:
KISUMU, Kenya, Nov 19 — A 16-year-old secondary school student has been killed by a hippopotamus while bathing with three friends at the shores of Lake Victoria in Rusinga Island, Homa Bay County.
The incident occurred on Wednesday evening at Kaswanga Beach in Kaswanga village, Suba North Constituen
items.text:
KISUMU, Kenya, Nov 19 — A 16-year-old secondary school student has been killed by a hippopotamus while bathing with three friends at the shores of Lake Victoria in Rusinga Island, Homa Bay County.
The incident occurred on Wednesday evening at Kaswanga Beach in Kaswanga village, Suba North Constituency, where the student had gone to swim with his friends.
The deceased, identified as Odhiambo, was a Grade 10 student at St Pius Uriri Senior Secondary School in Migori County.
Rusinga Central Location Chief Wilson Odoyo said the boys had not ventured far into the lake when the hippopotamus suddenly emerged from the water and attacked them.
“The boys had gone to bathe at the beach, and they had not gone far into the water when the hippo suddenly attacked them,” Odoyo said.
He said the animal caught Odhiambo as his friends managed to escape without injuries.
Odoyo added that the hippopotamus appeared to have been lurking close to the shoreline before charging at the group.
Fishermen who rushed to the scene attempted to rescue the teenager but were unable to save him after the animal dragged him underwater.
“The fishermen tried their best to rescue the boy, but their efforts were unsuccessful after the hippo dragged him underwater,” the chief said.
The incident has raised fresh concerns over the danger posed by hippopotamuses to communities living and working along Lake Victoria.
Odoyo urged residents, particularly fishermen, beach operators and young people, to exercise caution when accessing the lake and avoid bathing in areas frequented by the animals.
“We are appealing to residents living along the beaches to be very careful when carrying out their activities along the lake. The increasing presence of dangerous wild animals is putting people’s lives at risk,” he said.
He warned that encounters with wild animals could have fatal consequences, particularly for residents who regularly depend on the lake for domestic and economic activities.
The teenager’s body was later retrieved from the water and taken to Homa Bay County Hospital mortuary, where it was preserved pending a postmortem examination.

Initial reports said that one person had died, but some local media have reported
items.text:
Dozens missing after boat carrying 100 migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
- Published
Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a boat reportedly carrying about 100 migrants capsized off the coast.
Initial reports said that one person had died, but some local media have reported that at least four bodies have been recovered. Dozens of people are still missing.
Personal belongings were found on the badly damaged boat, which washed ashore near the village of Yenne, south of Dakar. Search operations continued throughout Wednesday and were due to resume on Thursday.
This comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off the coast of the north-western town of Thieppe killed at least 39 people, in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters.
Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, said the latest tragedy happened around 02:00 local time (02:00 GMT).
"Cries could be heard coming from the pirogue that were audible even from the beach," the AFP news agency quoted him as saying.
A survivor questioned by the police said there were about 100 people on the boat, including five women, the AFP reported.
Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings from the wreckage, including a school enrolment document.
At a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern about a renewed increase in irregular departure by migrants hoping to reach Europe.
He instructed the interior ministry to prepare a report examining the factors driving the dangerous journeys and proposing measures to tackle the problem.
Following last month's tragedy, Faye had urged Senegalese people not to risk their lives attempting the dangerous sea crossings.
Many thousands of people from West Africa have died or gone missing trying to flee conflict, authoritarian rule or poverty in recent years.
The UN's migration agency IOM said last month that it had recorded at least 454 deaths and disappearances off the West African coast this year alone.
It warned the figures were likely to be an underestimate, as many boats disappear without leaving survivors or a trace.
As it has become more difficult to reach Europe through North Africa, due to tighter controls and increased co-operation with European countries, migrants are increasingly targeting Spain's Canary Islands.
They often travel in wooden boats known as pirogues that are frequently overloaded and not suited to such long voyages across the Atlantic Ocean.
Most migrants arriving in the Canary Islands this year are from Senegal, according to the UN.
They are driven to leave home by limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks, according to the IOM.
On 7 November, El Hierro, one of the Canary islands, declared a state of emergency following a surge in migrant arrivals.
It said more than 3,300 people had reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of the month. This amounts to almost a third of the island's population.

items.text:
India: Nearly 50,000 evacuated as Cyclone Akvan nears the coast
Published November 19, 2026last updated November 19, 2026
What you need to know
- Protests hit parts of Bangladesh ahead of Sheikh Hasina's return, Muhammad Yunus' ancestral home set ablaze
- Odisha evacuates about 50,000 as Cyclone Akvan, the third severe storm in a month, nears the coast
- Prime Minister Modi chairs meeting of high-level ministers to review governance initiatives
Here is a roundup of headlines from India from Thursday, November 19:
Wellington: Nicholls hundred drags New Zealand back after Bumrah’s early blows
Henry Nicholls made an unbeaten 113 to help New Zealand recover from 70-5 to finish the first day of the first Test at 243-5 in Wellington on Thursday. India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bowl.
Jasprit Bumrah, playing his first Test in about a year, bowled New Zealand captain Tom Latham with the third ball of the match. He finished with 3-52 from 17 overs, adding Daryl Mitchell and Tom Blundell.
Nicholls and Glenn Phillips then added an unbroken 173 after lunch as the pitch eased and India's other pacers lost their lines. Nicholls' 12th Test hundred came from 188 balls, 141 of them dot balls.
Devdutt Padikkal dropped him on 102. Phillips was 94 not out.
"You play at a venue like this and against a team like India, it's a special occasion," AFP cited Nicholls as saying.
India's batting coach, Sitanshu Kotak, said the team's less experienced bowlers could learn from how Bumrah adjusted to New Zealand conditions, AFP reported.
Bangladesh: Awami League lockdown turns violent ahead of Hasina's return, Yunus's ancestral home torched
Parts of Bangladesh shut down Thursday as police reported two members of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) were killed and the ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus was set on fire.
The unrest comes ahead of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's planned return from exile in India next month, despite facing the death sentence there.
Her party, the Awami League, which was banned after Hasina was ousted, called for the nationwide "lockdown" after a week of protests over the government's rejection of her request for a new passport and identity card.
Police said two local BNP leaders were killed in Narail when Awami League activists attacked a BNP march, local media reported. It added that two other people, a local BNP leader and a transport worker, died in Faridpur and Pirojpur earlier this week.
Newspaper reports said suspected BNP activists attacked or set fire to the homes of two Awami League leaders in Dhaka.
Crude bombs went off in Dhaka before dawn and at least four people were wounded, the Press Trust of India reported. Reuters said 97 platoons of the Border Guard had been deployed across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur.
Authorities said flammable material was probably thrown into an unused ground-floor room of Yunus's Chattogram family home, and that relatives living upstairs were safe. At least 37 Grameen Bank branches and offices, which Yunus founded, have been targeted since November 10, the bank said.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said those behind the violence will be identified and prosecuted, and he accused Awami League leaders abroad of inciting it. Awami League leaders could not be reached for comment, Reuters said.
Cyclone Akvan: Odisha evacuates thousands as severe storm nears the coast
Odisha has evacuated tens of thousands of people ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is expected to cross the coast by noon Friday, the third severe cyclonic storm to threaten India's east coast in less than a month.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha with winds up to 110 kmph. The IMD now expects a severe cyclonic storm, not the very severe storm it projected earlier. Local media reported red alerts for heavy to extremely heavy rain in both states.
Reuters cited the chief minister's office, which said more than 47,000 people had been evacuated by Thursday. Local media put the figure at about 50,000 and said 3,000 cyclone shelters had been opened.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said most evacuees were from Ganjam district. Schools in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal are shut for three days from Thursday. Later, authorities announced that schools in Malkangiri, Rayagada and Koraput districts would also remain closed on Thursday and Friday.
"No evacuations in Andhra Pradesh yet," state disaster official Prakhar Jain told Reuters. "The storm has reduced in intensity."
Cyclone Arnab struck the region in late October and Cyclone Murasu earlier this month.
Welcome to our coverage
Hello!
This is Seerat from DW's Studio Delhi, bringing you the latest news from India, once again.
Odisha has announced school closures in multiple districts as Cyclone Akvan, the third severe storm to threaten India's east coast in a month, looks ready to make landfall.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired a meeting with his Council of Ministers — his top team for governance at New Delhi's Bharat Mandapam.
Meanwhile, in neighboring Bangladesh, supporters of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina have called for a "lockdown" after days of protests. The ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus was set on fire.
For this and more, follow our live blog.

items.title: US-led consortium wins Kenya’s Mrima Hill mineral tender
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 19 — The government has named winning bidders for three strategic mineral projects in Kwale, Samburu and Tharaka Nithi counties following the conclusion of a tendering process.
Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Hassan Ali Joho said the Ministry had issue
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 19 — The government has named winning bidders for three strategic mineral projects in Kwale, Samburu and Tharaka Nithi counties following the conclusion of a tendering process.
Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Hassan Ali Joho said the Ministry had issued Notices of Intention to Award to the highest-scoring responsive bidders after completing the evaluation and statutory procurement reviews.
Frontier Minerals Consortium, comprising Frontier Minerals LLC, Bunker Hill Mining Corp, ReElement Technologies and American Resources Corporation, was selected for the Mrima Hill Niobium, Rare Earth Elements and Other Minerals Project in Kwale County.
A joint venture between Fangda Special Steel Technology Co. Ltd and Sinohydro Corporation was selected for both the Kang’ura Chromite Development Project in Samburu County and the Kamacabi Copper Development Project in Tharaka Nithi County.
The tendering process did not produce responsive qualifying bids for the Lali Hills Manganese Project in Tana River County and the Kiritiri Coltan Project in Embu County, Joho said in a statement on Thursday.
The Ministry said the two projects would be addressed separately in accordance with the law.
Community consent before prospecting
Joho cautioned that the award of tenders did not automatically authorise the companies to commence prospecting, saying they must first complete community engagement and statutory licensing requirements.
“An award at the end of a tender process is not a licence to immediately break ground; rather, it is the gateway to meaningful local partnership and strict regulatory compliance,” he said.
The successful bidders must engage host communities, landowners, county leadership and other local stakeholders and obtain all requisite consents under the Mining Act (Cap. 306).
They must also submit applications for prospecting licences through the Ministry’s Online Mining Cadastre portal, attach the required consents and statutory documents, and pay the prescribed fees.
The applications will be subjected to independent scrutiny by the Mineral Rights Board, which will make recommendations before Joho grants the respective licences.
The Cabinet Secretary said the Government had prioritised identifying technically competent and financially capable investors before beginning formal community consent processes.
“Host communities deserve to know exactly who is coming to their locality, what their technical track record looks like, and whether they possess the real financial muscle to honour commitments on environmental safety, cultural heritage, local jobs, and community development,” he said.
How bidders were selected
The process began with an open Request for Expression of Interest published in March 2026 in the Kenya Gazette, The East African, MyGov Publication and the State Department for Mining website.
Shortlisted firms received detailed Requests for Proposals in July, followed by a mandatory pre-bid conference in August. Bids were opened on October 21 before undergoing preliminary, technical and financial evaluations.
The technical assessment considered geological and exploration expertise, mineral processing plans, local content, Kenyan employment commitments, environmental restoration, biodiversity management and cultural heritage protection. Bidders were required to attain a minimum technical score of 80 per cent.
The financial evaluation examined audited financial capacity, funded exploration investment plans and financial commitments to the State.
Joho said the process was intended to attract investors committed to local value addition, environmental protection and shared prosperity.
“Our commitment from the outset was to ensure that Kenya attracts only world-class, technically capable, and financially sound partners who share our vision for in-country value addition, environmental stewardship, and shared prosperity,” he said.
He invited residents and local leaders in Kwale, Samburu and Tharaka Nithi to participate in the upcoming engagements, urging successful bidders to approach communities with humility, transparency and respect.

The best European strikers this century - ranked by you

There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front o
items.text:
The best European strikers this century - ranked by you
- Published
Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.
There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.
This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.
Tens of thousands of you voted on the 20-man shortlist drawn up by our panel.
We then asked European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein to discuss your choices on the Euro Leagues podcast.
So from 10-1, here are the best European strikers this century - as voted for by you.
10. Karim Benzema
Karim Benzema comes in at number 10, the former Lyon and Real Madrid frontman's closest challengers coming from across the continent in the shape of Raul, Robin van Persie, Michael Owen and Miroslav Klose.
Laurens: "From a young age you could see he was something special. I know it was difficult at the beginning at Real Madrid, but in the post-Cristiano era he carried that team, wore the armband and won big titles and trophies by being decisive in big moments. Like I used to say 'Karim the dream'."
Honigstein: "The selflessness, the ability to work for the team. A sense of elegance and humility on the pitch, which is unusual in a goalscorer. I think he is unusual in that list. I think not many will define themselves through their teamwork and assists as much as their goals, but he was that player."
9. Ruud van Nistelrooy
Ruud van Nistelrooy edges Benzema, with whom he briefly overlapped at Real Madrid - the Dutchman teed up the Frenchman and scored himself in their only La Liga appearance together, before he left for Hamburg in January 2010 following injury problems.
The former PSV striker's most consistent spell, of course, came at Manchester United, where he scored 150 goals.
Honigstein: "He is the nicest guy but he never came across that way on the pitch. Typical trait of a striker, he would kill to score the goal. I think anyone who has grown up with him scoring goals, for United especially, must have a soft spot for him because he was a phenomenal poacher."
Laurens: "He was a strong player physically, and despite the lack of pace the awareness in the box was just very special even with all the injuries."
8. Zlatan Ibrahimovic
Zlatan Ibrahimovic slots in at eight, comfortably clear of Van Nistelrooy and Benzema. The Swede netted more than 500 times in a career that spanned Malmo, Ajax, Juventus, both Milans, Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Manchester United and LA Galaxy.
Balague: "He was a big-game player and that explains the league titles with PSG. Scoring four goals against England, the overhead kick. The personality thing has put him one or two places in this list, saying 'I am great, I am the best'. If you keep saying you're great it makes people stop and think."
Laurens: "The mentality of really believing he was the best and nobody was better than him, apart from maybe Brazilian Ronaldo, who was his idol growing up, and he would watch videos of him and try to replicate in his council estate. If you watch a highlight reel of his best goals he was incredible."
Honigstein: "What makes him unique among the strikers is his technique, You could see elements of martial arts in his goals. No-one scores goals like that."
7. Wayne Rooney
The first Englishman on the list, although the third to have represented Manchester United - it's the Old Trafford outfit's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney.
Honigstein: "I don't think there is anyone who would've watched English football at that time [early in his career] and not been enthralled by his game. The only downside is the combination of injuries and not the most professional lifestyle meant he did not fulfil his potential. He could've been Messi."
Balague: "What could have been, yes. He was the national team's record scorer too before Harry Kane took it. I find him to deserve this place as he had to adapt to a lot of strikers and he did it well. He had the ability to link up and score. He was very intelligent."
Laurens: "He is the most street footballer England has ever seen. There's no rules, that kind of anger you saw on the pitch. I don't think people in England realise how good he was."
6. Kylian Mbappe
What does becoming the all-time World Cup top goalscorer get you? Sixth place on the best European strikers this century list. The Real Madrid forward, 27, just misses out on the top five.
Laurens: "Maybe if we do this ranking again in a few years he will be higher. I would have had him top five, for sure. He has scored more than 400 goals. I don't think Messi and Ronaldo had scored that many at that age, so he's ahead. I don't know if he will play for as long as them but he hasn't done much wrong in his career."
Balague: "This list has to do what you feel about the player, not science - 22 goals in 22 appearances in World Cups and [Euro] Championships. He should be at least top three because of that. Great stats, but we're not in love with him."
Honigstein: "I don't think there is a forward that is as good as footballer as him in 2026. On that basis alone he should be higher, but people when they vote have other things in their head. The only way to win everyone over is to score more goals and win more World Cups for France, which I think is possible."
5. Erling Haaland
There was little between Mbappe and Erling Haaland, but it is Manchester City's prolific Norwegian who slips in at fifth. The 26-year-old has already scored more than 300 club goals and has a staggering 68 in 61 games for his country.
Balague: "Mbappe should be higher than him. Haaland scored 52 goals in 53 games [in 2022-23], that is astonishing, but he's gone 11 finals without scoring. We're talking about the best. items.summary:
Anthony Joshua: British heavyweight boxer becomes dad for second time but unable to see daughter until after Tyson Fury fight
Anthony Joshua says ongoing training camp for his fight against Tyson Fury on December 11 means he will not see his new-born daughter until the days after the fight; "It's no
items.text:
Anthony Joshua: British heavyweight boxer becomes dad for second time but unable to see daughter until after Tyson Fury fight
Anthony Joshua says ongoing training camp for his fight against Tyson Fury on December 11 means he will not see his new-born daughter until the days after the fight; "It's not ideal but she is in good hands", says Joshua, who describes daughter's arrival as a "big blessing"
Thursday 19 November 2026 11:17, UK
Anthony Joshua became a father for the second time after the birth of a daughter last weekend, although ongoing training for his fight against Tyson Fury means he is not able to see her until mid-December.
Joshua, whose son JJ was born in 2015, is currently in training camp in Marbella in preparation for his blockbuster all-British fight against Fury on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, and was unable to be at the birth.
Joshua says the arrival of his daughter, who has not yet been named, is "amazing" and "a big blessing" as the 37-year-old paid tribute to Nicole, the mother of both children.
- Opetaia withdraws from Wilder bout on Fury-AJ undercard
- Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📺
- Listen to the Toe2Toe podcast every week
While he has been able to have "many" FaceTime calls with mother and daughter in recent days, Joshua says he wished he would have been able to be there but preparations for the Fury fight mean mean he is currently "on a mission".
"It's not ideal but she is in good hands," Joshua said in an interview with The Sun.
"She's got an amazing mother, she's got amazing family round her and the people at the hospital, I heard they were amazing. I spoke to them and said thank you, so I'm pretty content at the minute that she's in good hands. But, for me, it would have been much better if I was able to be there.
"But I'm on duty at the minute and we're on a mission. I knew about this nine months ago so I made this commitment that I can't change, unfortunately, but there will be many more birthdays I'll be at, for sure."
Asked when he would likely meet her in person for the first time, Joshua said: "Probably December 12, December 13.
"I'll go and check in and rock her to sleep, let her hear my voice and let her feel my heartbeat, really. The basic stuff."
He said he would be a fully hands-on father.
"I'm going to do it all. I'm going to definitely do it all," he added.
"You might see me with some eye shadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll's playhouse just trying to do the right thing by her."
Joshua said he had wanted to become a father for a second time to "do something positive" after the "painful and traumatic" experience of last December's car crash in Nigeria that killed two members of his team, personal trainer Latif Ayodele, and strength and conditioning coach Sina Ghami.
"After the year that I'm coming off I wanted to do something positive," said Joshua, who was injured in the crash.
"I wanted to give JJ the opportunity to be an older brother. One day I won't be here and he'll have a sibling that he can turn to, be with and plan their future together. It's nice to have a sibling that they can lean on each other when needed, when me and his mum aren't here one day in the future."
The British boxer added: "Nicole is doing good. She is healthy. She said it was an amazing experience. She said it was easier than JJ and she's much prettier than JJ, so she's happy! She's already deeply in love with her."

items.summary:
Trump meets Putin and Xi as trilateral US, Russia, China talks begin
US president calls both Putin and Xi a ‘friend’ in separate meetings at APEC, ahead of rare three-way talks.
United States President Donald Trump is meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts for highly anticipated trilatera
items.text:
Trump meets Putin and Xi as trilateral US, Russia, China talks begin
US president calls both Putin and Xi a ‘friend’ in separate meetings at APEC, ahead of rare three-way talks.
United States President Donald Trump is meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts for highly anticipated trilateral talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin began talks on the sidelines of the summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday in an unprecedented gathering of the world’s three superpowers.
The talks between the leaders of the world’s largest nuclear powers are unlikely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. But the meeting has unnerved smaller countries that fear their interests might be disregarded.
Ahead of the trilateral gathering, Trump held separate bilateral meetings with both Xi and Putin on Thursday.
The US president described Xi as a “friend” and said Washington and Beijing enjoyed a “special relationship”.
“As long as the two of us are in charge, I don’t think we’ll have a problem,” Trump said in opening remarks at his meeting with the Chinese leader. He also boasted that “no other countries can do what we can”.
Trump said the US has done “amazing” things in the past two years, since he returned to power, while praising China for many of its gains over several years.
Xi, meanwhile, said that he remained committed to working with Trump to steer ties between their countries on the “correct course”.
Relations between Beijing and Washington have been stable and improving, Xi said to Trump at the start of their third meeting this year, which lasted for about an hour.
“We have established a new definition of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, giving it new substance based on respect, fairness and reciprocity,” Xi said.
Ahead of the bilateral meeting, Trump said the Board of Trade that he and the Chinese president agreed to form at their Beijing summit in May has brought balance to the two countries’ relationship. He said the US and China had split their tariffs in a “fair way”.
Putin ‘is my friend’
Earlier in the day, during talks with Putin, Trump also called the Russian leader a “friend”.
“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they’ll come out of this,” Trump told Putin.
A video published by the White House showed the two leaders shaking hands and Trump briefly whispering to Putin at the start of their meeting.
In another video posted by the White House Rapid Response X account, Trump was shown pointing at Putin and saying, “He’s my friend.”
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said the two leaders “discussed the conflict in Ukraine and bilateral relations issues”.
“The meeting between the Russian and US leaders went well,” Ushakov said, according to Russia’s state news agency TASS, adding that Putin left the talks “in an excellent” mood.
“There were no particularly significant statements made at the Putin-Trump talks; everyone is preparing for the trilateral meeting,” he added.
‘High-stakes diplomacy’
Thursday also features the main event of the APEC summit, as representatives of the 21 Pacific Rim economies gather for discussions that will include high-stakes diplomacy, Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu said, reporting from Shenzhen.
“Xi Jinping, who spoke at the banquet last night during the opening ceremony, said the discussion will centre on promoting mutual openness, innovation-driven growth and results-oriented cooperation,” said Yu.
On the US-China-Russia talks, James Bays, Al Jazeera’s diplomatic editor, said that when it comes to Trump, “his personal role always matters to him”.
But, he added, “something worth bearing in mind: you have three leaders here, Trump, Xi, and Putin. Putin has been in power; he’s been in the main driving seat in Moscow for 26 years; Xi’s been there for 14 years; and they know President Trump only has 26 more months.”
Speaking to Fox News earlier on Thursday, Trump highlighted the pomp surrounding his arrival. Xi greeted Air Force One on the airport tarmac on Wednesday, which contrasted with the more muted greetings offered to other leaders.
“This is a great president, one of the great presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody,” Trump said when asked what he wanted to get out of the trilateral summit.
Trump has insisted that nuclear arms control be a central topic of the meeting, despite Beijing’s repeated objections to talks on the issue with Washington and Moscow, which have far larger nuclear arsenals.

items.title: Killer building collapses expose Kenya’s regulatory rot
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 19 – Kenya’s growing trail of deadly building collapses is exposing deep failures in construction regulation, with fresh revelations of forged approval documents in Eastleigh and unanswered safety concerns surrounding Bridge Port Apartments in South C raising questions about the s
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 19 – Kenya’s growing trail of deadly building collapses is exposing deep failures in construction regulation, with fresh revelations of forged approval documents in Eastleigh and unanswered safety concerns surrounding Bridge Port Apartments in South C raising questions about the safety of property buyers and occupants.
The crisis has placed the National Construction Authority (NCA), county governments, Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK) and National Environment Management Authority (NEMA) under scrutiny over alleged regulatory negligence, weak inspections and failure to enforce building standards.
In South C, residents are demanding urgent intervention over the 15-storey Bridge Port Apartments, which neighbours the 16-storey building along Muhoho Avenue that collapsed in January 2026, killing two people.
The South C Residents Association has alleged that Bridge Port Apartments, owned by Kenneth Nyachae, brother of former East Africa Court of Justice judge Charles Nyachae, was approved for only 10 floors and that its structural pillars were damaged during the neighbouring building’s collapse.
In a May 11, 2026 letter to Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome, residents demanded the release of an investigation report and an independent structural assessment to establish whether the apartments remained safe for occupation.
They also sought a public safety certificate or appropriate enforcement action, warning that occupants could be exposed to danger if the alleged structural damage remained unaddressed. The residents say no action has been taken.
The concerns have been compounded by revelations surrounding the October 23 collapse of an 18-storey building along Ninth Street in Eastleigh, which killed eight people, injured several others and exposed apparent loopholes in Nairobi’s development approval system.
In a statement, the South C Residents Association chairman, Abdi Karim Hassan, demanded that the Cabinet Secretary release the multi-agency inquiry report into the collapse of Plot 68/1306 and provide an update on the status of Bridge Port Apartments.
The residents also demanded a public safety certification or demolition order for the adjacent 15-storey building owned by Bridge Port Apartments Limited.
“This building was approved for 10 floors but stands at 15, with documented structural damage to its pillars,” the statement said.
image
Caption: Protesters outside Ardhi House demanding accountability following the South C building collapse that claimed two lives in Nairobi, April 20, 2026.
Appearing before the Nairobi County Assembly’s Urban Planning Committee, Assistant Director for Development Control Fredrick Ochanda disclosed that City Hall had never approved the building’s architectural or structural plans.
He told the committee that developer John Mutie Musyoki had initially obtained approval to change the property’s use from private residential to commercial and residential development but had failed to secure construction approval.
Architect Emmanuel Mwangi Maina submitted an application on November 25, 2024, for a building comprising a basement and 15 floors. The application was unsuccessful after an invoice of Sh2 million remained unpaid.
A second application submitted on November 14, 2025, attracted an invoice of Sh1.1 million, which was paid. However, it was not approved because of inadequate parking, proposed basement shops and failure to obtain Kenya Civil Aviation Authority clearance.
“As of now, there is no application that has been approved,” Ochanda told the committee.
He further disclosed that documents allegedly presented to the NCA to demonstrate county approval were forged.
“An application was made to us, but it did not meet the minimum requirements. Regarding the question of NCA approval, the letters in question did not originate from us. They were forgeries,” he said.
Yet the NCA had registered the project on July 30, 2025, under registration number 53128815710410, listing 9th Street Plaza Limited as developer and Stromax Holdings EA Limited as contractor.
The revelations raise questions about how construction proceeded to 18 floors without county approval and why enforcement agencies failed to stop it.
The County Assembly committee, chaired by Baba Dogo MCA Geoffrey Majiwa, also expressed concern over the failure of the developer, contractor and some county officials to honour summonses. Governor Johnson Sakaja’s Chief of Staff David Njoroge and adviser Osman Khalif Abdi were among those asked to appear.
“In an inquiry, when you are adversely mentioned, you are summoned to come and clear your name,” Majiwa said, insisting that nobody should be condemned unheard.
Acting Director of Planning and Compliance Tom Achar had also alleged political interference by powerful individuals in City Hall’s approval processes.
The disasters are not isolated. On November 13, an eight-storey building near Nairobi’s Mombasa Road and SGR terminus collapsed, killing six people and leaving five rescued.
Other incidents in 2026 in Karen, Shauri Moyo, Kibra and Kericho claimed several lives, while a retaining-wall collapse along Riverside Drive killed four people and injured 11.
In the Eastleigh tragedy, four people were rescued alive, while three others remained unaccounted for when the search was called off.
A compilation by Stats Kenya puts reported building collapses between January 2020 and November 2026 at 84, resulting in 102 deaths and 138 injuries. The Architects Association of Kenya has previously warned about non-compliance, inadequate professional oversight and weak enforcement.
Under the regulatory framework, county governments approve building plans and issue development permits, the NCA registers construction projects and monitors compliance, EBK regulates engineers and engineering firms, while NEMA oversees environmental compliance.

items.text:
Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh and south
Material damage was reported after debris fell following the latest Houthi strikes launched towards Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis says it has intercepted missiles fired towards Riyadh and Saudi Arabia’s southern region after a loud boom was heard in the capital.
The attacks on Thursday are the latest in weeks of strikes by the Yemeni armed group targeting Saudi military, civilian and oil infrastructure.
Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki said on X that its forces “dealt with” a Houthi missile threat launched towards Riyadh.
An initial assessment showed debris had fallen and that material damage had been reported, he added, saying the extent of the damage was still being determined.
Hours later, in a separate post, the spokesman said air defences intercepted and destroyed four ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), towards the southern region, bordering Yemen.
The coalition said it had earlier also destroyed a ballistic missile launchpad used in the attempted attacks on Riyadh.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for targeting vital sites in the Saudi capital on Thursday, including the international airport and the financial centre, as well as Khamis Mushait and Abha city in the south, where alerts were sounded.
A Saudi aircraft, meanwhile, carried out air raids on the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital, Sanaa, earlier on Thursday, the group-run Saba news agency reported, without providing further details.
The latest attacks in Saudi Arabia coincided with an announcement by Yemeni government forces that they carried out about 750 air strikes and operations against the Houthis on several fronts, including in Taiz and Lahij, where the humanitarian situation is worsening day by day.
Earlier on Thursday, the United Nations children’s agency, UNICEF, said in a statement that “more than 330,000 people, including an estimated 174,000 children, have been displaced since the beginning of the renewed military escalations”.
“The number of casualties is likely to increase as renewed fighting continues around densely populated areas, particularly in Taiz” and Lahij, UNICEF said.
Meanwhile, Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council issued a decision designating the Houthi group a “terrorist” organisation on Thursday. It said anyone who cooperates with the group will face prosecution and punishment, with penalties that could include execution or prison terms of 30 years or more, Al Jazeera’s Yasser Hassan reported from Taiz.
Humanitarian organisations have released new figures on the casualties in the war, as fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has intensified since the group captured strategic areas along Yemen’s Red Sea coast last month.
The World Health Organization said this week that the death toll from the latest escalation that began in August has reached 2,260, with 10,519 wounded.
The renewed conflict between the two sides has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce that largely halted the exchange of attacks between the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government, and the Houthis, who control the most populous parts of the country.

items.title: Maine Road offer non-league haven to fans of scandal-hit Manchester City
items.summary:
It began with a timely message on social media. “We’ve seen the posts. We’ve read the comments. If all the recent conversation has made you curious about the other team in Manchester playing in sky blue, come and see us.”
It was a direct response to the news of a guilty verdict in the Premier League
items.text:
It began with a timely message on social media. “We’ve seen the posts. We’ve read the comments. If all the recent conversation has made you curious about the other team in Manchester playing in sky blue, come and see us.”
It was a direct response to the news of a guilty verdict in the Premier League’s financial fair play case against Manchester City and it came from the 10th-tier (step six) club Maine Road, who carry City’s colours and a near-identical badge, as well as the name of City’s previous home.
Maine Road stadium was demolished in 2003-04 and replaced by houses but two miles away, in a corner of Chorlton-cum-Hardy, Maine Road FC are playing in front of about 100 people on a cool November Saturday. The high-stakes surroundings of the Premier League seem a fair distance away, but Maine Road – founded in 1955 in Rusholme as a Manchester City supporters’ club team – have never professed to be City.
“There is FC United and Manchester United, who are intrinsically linked in terms of why that club exists,” says Rob McKay, Maine Road women’s head coach, watching as a fan as the men’s side draw 0-0 with Halewood Apollo in the North West Counties League First Division North. “This is not a protest club. The links with City have ebbed and flowed over the years. It’s just that they were playing out of the Maine Road social club when it formed.”
The chair and director Alex Simmonds, who arrived in the summer, has big ambitions for Maine Road. He believes the fallout from City’s legal battle with the Premier League could help attract a new audience.
“It was a bit of a statement,” Simmonds says of that social media post. “We came across a lot of comments when the news came out and a lot were saying: ‘Well, we’ll stop watching City if they get relegated or if anything happens, and we’ll just go to Maine Road.’ That came up in quite a few conversations online.”
Simmonds admits there has not yet been a huge rise in crowd numbers, with City fans, perhaps understandably, staying defiantly loyal to their club, who have appealed against the independent commission’s verdict. His priority is to regenerate Maine Road. “For me coming into the club, it was about trying to get people to see that we are here,” he says. “To get in touch with the community and to get fans down here, so no matter who you support in the Premier League or Championship or whatever, we are here.”
Maine Road offer free entry to anyone with a season ticket for a Premier League or EFL club, hoping to boost numbers during international breaks or when other Greater Manchester teams play away. Simmonds is helping to fund a multimillion-pound renovation of St Margaret’s Community Centre, which serves as Maine Road’s clubhouse. The club are also launching a new website and a scheme to hand out thousands of free tickets to local primary schools.
Will that, combined with potential disillusionment after any City punishment, bring fans flocking to Maine Road? “I think it will,” Simmonds says, “but only if people know that there’s a difference between a Premier League Man City and a Maine Road at step six. If they come with ideas that we are going to be a City or even one of the bigger semi-pro teams … we’re not quite there yet. But their support would help.”
Non-league football in Greater Manchester has enjoyed a significant surge in popularity since Covid, so Maine Road find themselves in a crowded marketplace. McKay says: “West Didsbury and Chorlton are down the road and they get 1,000. Droylsden get huge crowds, Ashton United get huge crowds, Curzon Ashton are getting reasonable crowds. There’s so much football.”
Simmonds believes the connection with City, however loose, should help Maine Road gradually gain a foothold. City’s former training ground at Platt Lane is a stone’s throw from Brantingham Road, where Maine Road play. City’s academy teams have played at Maine Road’s ground, as well as at nearby St Bede’s College.
Another connection is the fact Maine Road are managed by a former City player in Leon Mike, who made his only City start at the old Maine Road in 2001 under Kevin Keegan.
“People make jokes about the Etihad not being full, but genuinely, a lot of times you speak to City fans, they’ll say it’s too expensive,” says Mike. “Premier League, FA Cup, League Cup, Champions League, that’s a lot of games to go to. Whereas on a Saturday here it will cost you £6 to attend and you can have a pint and some food.”
There is optimism among those most closely connected with Maine Road that the club will soon experience growth. “We gained 9,000 followers across the platforms just on the back of that one social media post,” Simmonds says. “It was surprising – I didn’t think it would do that – but social media is really powerful. We’re definitely going to try and stay in that conversation and get people coming through.”

The Premier League is back after the recent international break and the Sky Sports football writers dissect all the major talking points ahead of another busy weekend's action.
Man City vs Fulham: Cottagers ideal opponents to get City back to winning ways
Are Man City in crisis heading into Saturday lunchtime's clash against Fulham, with Enzo Maresca's side having lost their previous three Premier League contests to lose top spot to Arsenal?
Those trio of reverses against Aston Villa, Brighton and, just prior to the international break, Nottingham Forest, mean City have now lost as many times as in their previous 36 league outings.
Since the start of 2007-08, though, City have only been beaten in four successive top-flight games on two occasions, in August 2008 and December 2024, and it would take a massive leap of faith to suggest Fulham are the team to inflict such ignominy on them this weekend.
In fact, if Maresca could pick one side to face to get back to winning ways, it would be Fulham, who City have got the better of in each of their last 17 Premier League encounters, scoring at least twice each time.
