items.summary:
Lauren Price hopes making undisputed history could lead her to Claressa Shields showdown: 'I want the big fights'
Olympic gold medallist Lauren Price wants to test herself against Claressa Shields, Chantelle Cameron and Mikaela Mayer; Price will become Wales' first undisputed world champion in the f
items.text:
Lauren Price hopes making undisputed history could lead her to Claressa Shields showdown: 'I want the big fights'
Olympic gold medallist Lauren Price wants to test herself against Claressa Shields, Chantelle Cameron and Mikaela Mayer; Price will become Wales' first undisputed world champion in the four-belt era if she beats Michaela Kotaskova and hopes victory can lead to American star Shields
Wednesday 18 November 2026 18:02, UK
Lauren Price believes becoming an undisputed champion could lead her to a showdown with American star Claressa Shields.
Price faced off with Shields after her last fight but no agreement has been reached for them to box.
Shields has been an undisputed champion in multiple divisions and has returned to middleweight after a period as the undisputed heavyweight champion.
Price, like Shields, won the Olympic gold medal at middleweight. She's unbeaten as a professional too. On Friday Price looks to add the now vacant WBO welterweight title to the WBA, WBC and IBF belts she already holds when she fights Michaela Kotaskova.
If she wins she will become Wales' first undisputed champion in the four-belt era.
"It hasn't sunk in yet," Price told Sky Sports. "When I turned over, that's the dream to become undisputed. I can honestly say if I achieve that on Friday then I've ticked every accolade in boxing.
"Regardless of the belts on the line, you step through the ropes and it's another fight. I just let the boxing do the talking and make sure I get that win and I win in style."
If Price does go undisputed at welterweight, moving up through divisions will be the natural next step. Shields remains a target though that fight is yet to come to fruition.
"It has to make sense on both ends," Price said. "I'm giving away weight, fine. But it was in her back garden, I wanted to come back to Wales as well.
"I believe it will happen."
On December 24 Chantelle Cameron and Mikaela Mayer, who vacated the WBO welterweight title, will rematch for the WBA, WBC and WBO super-welter championships. Price has an eye on fighting the winner.
"They're both great. But I believe Chantelle will win that fight again and that's a great fight for British boxing, I'm 100 percent up for it," Price said.
"I think right now obviously myself, Cameron, Mayer's in there [the pound-for-pound list] and obviously Shields. For me we're the big names and that's what I want, I want the big fights."

items.title: Hamilton denies lack of trust with Ferrari after strategy issues
items.summary:
Lewis Hamilton denies lack of trust with Ferrari after ignoring instructions from pit wall twice in recent races
Lewis Hamilton ignored instructions from his Ferrari team to pit at recent races in Singapore and Brazil; the Brit insists there is no trust issue; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky S
items.text:
Lewis Hamilton denies lack of trust with Ferrari after ignoring instructions from pit wall twice in recent races
Lewis Hamilton ignored instructions from his Ferrari team to pit at recent races in Singapore and Brazil; the Brit insists there is no trust issue; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
Thursday 19 November 2026 06:13, UK
Lewis Hamilton has insisted there is no lack of trust between himself and his Ferrari team despite having overridden orders from the pit wall twice in recent races.
At the Singapore Grand Prix in October and the Sao Paulo Grand Prix earlier this month, Hamilton ignored instructions to pit, with his decision costing him places on both occasions.
The incidents followed several moments earlier in the season where Hamilton had been left frustrated by strategic decisions from Ferrari that failed to optimise his chances.

Asked ahead of this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix whether taking matters into his own hands was indicative of a lack of trust, Hamilton insisted he was pleased with the work of his race engineer Carlo Santi.
The seven-time world champion said: "No, it's definitely not trusting. I think it's just we're constantly working on our communication. I think that it's been a lot better this year.
"Carlo has done an amazing job, and I think there's been a couple of times where it's just those particular two times was not, particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed, and I got the call at the last minute.
"And we'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united and working, I think in the right direction."
'No concerns about racing Leclerc'
Hamilton has also had to handle controversy with his team-mate Charles Leclerc, after a first-lap clash between the pair at the Mexico City Grand Prix resulted in something of a public fall out.
Hamilton was highly critical of Leclerc for aggressively attempting to challenge him for the lead on the first lap, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen taking advantage of the squabble to win a race that Ferrari likely would have claimed a one-two in had their drivers held position.
Both Hamilton and Leclerc said that a conversation in Brazil the week after the incident had resolved the situation, and the Brit on Wednesday reiterated his confidence in their working relationship moving forwards.
"I think Charles is a great driver," Hamilton said. "I think, as I said, the detail we went into about stuff like that in terms of when we close the visor, it's very clear we understand each other.
"We understand each other's boundaries and the ultimate goal, which is to get the best result for the team.
"So, I don't feel that that will be a problem moving forwards, and I have no concerns or worries about racing him. I don't think he does with me either."
Can Ferrari challenge in Las Vegas?
Hamilton admitted he is unsure whether Ferrari will be able to challenge for victory in Las Vegas given the circuit is unlikely to suit their car.
The circuit's long straight could expose Ferrari's power unit weaknesses, while the cold temperatures could lead to issues heating up their tyres sufficiently.
Hamilton said: "We've had a car that's been quick through corners. Obviously, yeah, you have the long straight here. I don't know how that's going to be for us.
"We'll do the best job we can, but hopefully we can make up some of the time maybe in some of the corners. We'll have to wait and see."
Regardless of how competitive Ferrari are, Hamilton says the team will use this weekend, and the upcoming final two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, to attempt to optimise their plans for the start of the 2027 season.
"This is a period of time… we don't have any new components to test, but this is definitely a really important data point for us to understand and make some changes setup wise, and try some things that we can potentially try to see if everything's working, if there's different elements of the car that we can remove or add, thinking about next year," he said.
"There's some big changes for next year. But otherwise, right now we have to focus on maintain second in the constructors' championship."

items.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
items.summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.
Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying
items.text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.
Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.
The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit.
“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.
For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”
He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”
He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”
But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”
When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”
He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”
In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

items.text:
Former United States men's coach and current San Jose Earthquakes manager Bruce Arena called out U.S. Soccer as the federation searches for Mauricio Pochettino's replacement.
Pochettino was confirmed as Manchester United's new head coach on Nov. 13, leaving the USMNT after more than two years in charge.
U.S. Soccer said the federation would begin the search for a new coach with U23 manager Steve Cherundolo overseeing a December camp and friendly against Jamaica next month.
"In my view, they don't have a clue what they are doing," Arena said on Wednesday when asked about the search.
Pochettino led the United States to a 2-0 victory over Haiti on Nov. 17 in his final game in charge before immediately departing for England. Combined with a 6-0 win against Haiti in the first leg, the U.S. advanced 8-0 on aggregate to the Concacaf Nations League finals.
This wasn't the first time that Arena, who served as USMNT coach from 1998 to 2006 and again from 2016 to 2017, was critical of the hiring of Pochettino. The San Jose Earthquakes manager said in 2025 that a non-American lacked the necessary understanding of the country's culture to manage the Americans.
"You know if you look at every national team in the world, the coach is usually a domestic coach," Arena said on the "Unfiltered Soccer" podcast with former USMNT stalwarts Landon Donovan and Tim Howard in 2025. "I think when you're a national team coach, you need to know your environment, you need to know the animals you coach, and we're lacking that. If you're an American coaching the U.S. team, you know the culture, you know the pride and how important the national team is. I think when you bring in somebody from the outside, they don't understand it, especially in our country, because we're so different."
Arena currently stands as the USMNT coach with most victories recorded in his tenure. During his first stint, Arena managed 71 wins, 30 losses and 29 draws, and led the Americans to the quarterfinals of the 2002 World Cup. He returned in 2016 and took that tally to 81 wins, but infamously fell short of guiding the team to qualification for the 2018 World Cup.
Arena is preparing the San Jose Earthquakes for its round one matchup with Houston Dynamo FC in round one of the 2026 MLS playoffs.
"We played Houston twice this year," Arena said on Wednesday. "They know us, we know them. So there'll be no surprises. It will be a battle, like any playoff series in any sport. It'll be strongly challenging. We're hopeful that the home field advantage means something."
San Jose hosts Houston in game one of the best-of-three series on Nov. 24.

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.

A plane carry
items.text:
Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.
Pochettino's final act in charge of the United States national side was a 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday night.
A plane carrying Pochettino arrived at Manchester Airport on Wednesday afternoon. He headed to the club's training ground, Carrington, as the replacement for the sacked Michael Carrick before his first game leading United on Sunday against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.
On Tuesday night, Pochettino was told by former Manchester City and United States player DaMarcus Beasley that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue."
He responded: "You will see. Give me time.
"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it's adrenalin you want to feel. We need to add our common sense... we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing."
Pochettino added: "The mentality is to learn from everyone. You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us every day, we are much better coaching staff now.
"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."
Upon arrival at Carrington, Pochettino said he is "very excited to be here. It's an honour. It's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Yes, looking forward to start to work."
United have confirmed Jesus Perez, Miguel D'Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino as Pochettino's staff.
Mauricio Pochettino starts work at Man United on Wednesday
Pochettino was also asked about whether he can improve United's running statistics, which were criticised by ex-boss Carrick after a drab 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.
In response to Bruno Fernandes' questioning of the team's tactics, Carrick said: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."
Pochettino said on Tuesday night: "What I can talk in general, football is very complex and I think it's not important if you run or not run.
"You need to run well, you need to run with an objective, you need to run together. Then you need to play, you need to know what you need to do, you need to express your talent. The mindsets are so important."
Pochettino led the U.S. to the round of 16 at last summer's World Cup on home soil.
But he is now returning to the Premier League where he has previously coached Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

items.title: USWNT's Emma Hayes on role in USMNT coach search: 'Through a technical lens'
items.summary:
United States women's national team coach Emma Hayes said that she's committed to helping with a thorough search for the next men's national team coach after the recent exit of Mauricio Pochettino.
On Tuesday, Pochettino managed his last game for the U.S. men, a 2-0 win over Haiti in the quarterfina
items.text:
United States women's national team coach Emma Hayes said that she's committed to helping with a thorough search for the next men's national team coach after the recent exit of Mauricio Pochettino.
On Tuesday, Pochettino managed his last game for the U.S. men, a 2-0 win over Haiti in the quarterfinals of the Concacaf Nations League, before departing to Manchester United.
"I'm very embedded into the federation, and I work really closely with [U.S. Soccer CEO] JT [Batson], in particular, and even more so with [U.S. Soccer COO] Dan [Helfrich] as we're growing to develop the American soccer movement and JT asked if I would be involved as a technical voice, to be involved with the process," Hayes said.
"I feel confident in the group of people that have been put together to create a thorough process to select the next men's national team coach, and my role is merely to support that through a technical lens, knowing I do this job at least, albeit with the women's team, and that I've coached for a number of years and can offer some of that insight into the application of what to look for and why."
The federation announced last week that Hayes would be part of a group that would look for the next men's coach.
"Batson and U.S. Soccer Chief Operating Officer Dan Helfrich, alongside the soccer leadership team at U.S. Soccer that includes Emma Hayes and Oguchi Onyewu, will lead the search for the next USMNT head coach, drawing on input from leaders across U.S. Soccer and the global soccer landscape," said U.S. Soccer. "The Federation will consider candidates from a broad range of backgrounds."
Hayes is currently preparing for a Concacaf W Championship quarterfinal against El Salvador on Nov. 27. The winner of the single-leg knockout match will qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
Pochettino was asked on Tuesday if he'll be available to help the U.S. Soccer Federation pick his successor, but the Argentine said he wouldn't be participating in that process.
"I think it's not my job. And for sure they have the capacity and the knowledge to find the right people with the right profile," he said. "I don't know how to measure my colleagues and I think it's not my job.
"More than two years ago they signed Emma Hayes [for the U.S. women's national team] and then Mauricio Pochettino. I think they have good eyes. They have good taste of football."
Former U.S. international Steve Cherundolo will oversee the final USMNT game of the year against Jamaica on Dec. 13 in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
The U.S. will play its next competitive match in late March at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles against Mexico for the Nations League semifinals.

Coffey, a starting midfielder for the U.S. during its 2024 Olympic gold medal run, ha
items.text:
Midfielder Sam Coffey has been named to the United States women's national team's World Cup qualifying roster that will assemble for training camp later this month, marking her first time with the team since April.
Coffey, a starting midfielder for the U.S. during its 2024 Olympic gold medal run, had a minor knee operation in the spring that kept her out of the past two international windows.
The U.S. will be without stalwart defender Naomi Girma again due to ongoing recovery from a series of calf injuries.
Girma also last played for the U.S. in a series of exhibitions against Japan in April.
On Wednesday, U.S. head coach Emma Hayes announced her 23-player roster for the World Cup qualifying event.
The U.S. will play El Salvador on Nov. 27 in the quarterfinals of the single-elimination Concacaf tournament in Mansfield, Texas.
All four quarterfinal winners automatically qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup, while the losers go into a play-in bracket for a change to advance to the global playoff.
About Girma's injury, Hayes said she was working closely with Chelsea.
"I've been speaking with Naomi a lot in the last few weeks," Hayes said in Wednesday's news conference. "I think there's been a really good club and country collaboration to get it right, because it's critical, and it's critical for a career that no detail is too small to be able to do that. I think in an ideal world we wouldn't be in the position that we're in.
"But listen, the human body reacts and responds to different stimulus in different ways, and I think Naomi has certainly grown an appreciation for not just taking a key role in her rehab, but being really thoughtful around and intuitive about a body, in relation to that.
"But we want to be right. We want to get it right. It's not about being first. I don't think we can afford --- anyone --- Naomi, Chelsea, USA, we have to make sure we are incredibly thorough to ensure that Naomi gets back on the pitch as soon as possible."
Angel City FC defender Evelyn Shores returns to the roster after receiving her first senior call-up last month for games against Spain (she did not play in a game).
Shores is just the second uncapped player in USWNT history to be named to a World Cup qualifying roster.
NWSL Golden Boot winner Ashley Sanchez and fellow forward Mallory Swanson also return to the roster.
Both players made their returns to the field for the U.S. against Spain and scored in the U.S.' 2-2 draw with the world's top team on Oct. 13.
"It's been a great year of growth and learning for our team, and for a long time the focus has been on qualifying for the World Cup, so now that time has arrived," Hayes said in a statement.
"I want to see relentless consistency from our players, individually and as a team, and I want us to be elite in both penalty boxes. If we can achieve that, I'm confident those performances will carry us through to meet our standards and goals. This is my first Concacaf event and the first for many of our players, so we're all looking forward to the experience."
Only seven players on the roster have World Cup qualifying experience, with only three of them -- Swanson and midfielders Lindsey Heaps and Rose Lavelle -- playing in multiple qualifying tournaments.
"Qualifying for a major tournament, first and foremost, I'll be leaning on our experienced players," Hayes said. "They know how to do this, and they've been with us the longest to be able to deliver that, and I think [also] for the less experienced players who have had a good body of work in the last couple of years, so we know what we need to do.
"We need to just make sure we come into camp with really clear mind about those things. Focus on the only game in front of us."
Goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn also returns to the roster after her outstanding performance for the Utah Royals in the NWSL quarterfinals earlier this month.
Utah teammate and defender Kate Del Fava also returns after receiving her first call-up and first cap against Spain on Oct. 13.
Forwards Jaedyn Shaw and Ally Sentnor, who had been regular USWNT call-ups in recent years, are again absent from the senior roster.
Hayes reiterated that no player has a guaranteed roster spot for the World Cup next year.
"We don't want players that are in our group that are in a place where they're not fighting to improve every day or be as competitive as they could possibly be," she said.
"But I think when players have stacked and accumulated a lot of experience over a period of time, that is always going to put them in a steady position. But it doesn't guarantee anything.
"I will be unafraid to leave anybody off that plane if I don't feel that they are applying themselves to put ourselves in the best possible position to compete, which is why this upcoming camp, our job is to qualify for the World Cup, and so everything we have worked towards is ensuring that every player that comes into camp makes sure they lift their level."

The England international, who was part of the Lionesses' 2022 and '25 European Championships squad, spent the last three seasons playing for Gotham FC, winning multipl
items.text:
Jess Carter is trading the east coast of the U.S. for the west after signing a deal with Bay FC, the NWSL side announced Wednesday.
The England international, who was part of the Lionesses' 2022 and '25 European Championships squad, spent the last three seasons playing for Gotham FC, winning multiple trophies including the NWSL Championship in 2025.
Carter, who was a free agent, has a contract with Bay FC that runs through 2028 with an option for 2029, the club said in a release.
"Coming to Bay FC is a new challenge, and that's something I'm excited about," Carter said in the release. "I've been fortunate to be part of some successful teams, and I know how much work goes into winning. I'm looking forward to getting to know this group, earning the trust of my teammates and doing my part to help us move forward."
Carter, 29, was a fixture at the heart of Gotham's defense in 2026, playing all 30 games during the regular season and starting both matches in the NWSL playoffs. Defending champions Gotham were eliminated in the semifinal by the Kansas City Current.
"Jess has consistently demonstrated her quality in championship-winning environments at both club and international level," said Bay FC chief football officer Paul Green. "Having worked with her at Chelsea, I've seen her development and the professionalism she brings every day. She will bring valuable experience to Bay FC, and we're delighted to welcome her to the club."
Before joining Gotham in 2024, Carter was part of a Chelsea side that won five consecutive Women's Super League titles.
Carter has made 56 appearances for England and was on the 2023 World Cup team that lost to Spain in the final. She was recently picked in the squad that will face Ukraine in a December doubleheader that serves as a qualifier for the 2027 World Cup.
Information from ESPN Global Research was used in this report.

items.text:
Manchester United are prepared to mount legal action if they find evidence that JJ Gabriel has been illegally approached by other clubs while under contract, sources have told ESPN.
Gabriel announced his departure from Old Trafford with a video posted on social media on Tuesday. Sources have told ESPN that United were unaware of the announcement until it was published.
United still hold Gabriel's registration and sources have told ESPN there has been no contact with any governing body about transferring the 16-year-old's registration to another club.
A verbal agreement is in place for Gabriel to sign for Real Madrid. He can join a club within the European Union as a domestic or EU player, bypassing non-EU foreign player quotas, because he has an EU passport.
Real Madrid were approached for comment by ESPN but have not yet responded.
The teenager has not been back to Carrington since walking out in September.
Sources have told ESPN that United staff have made a number of attempts to check on Gabriel's welfare, but have not been able to make contact with his family.
United, according to sources, believe Gabriel's family and representatives may have held meetings with rival clubs as early as last summer.
Gabriel refused a request from United to train with the academy at the start of preseason before joining the first-team squad on a full time basis. A number of demands were also made by his representatives ahead of the season.
They included Gabriel playing at least 20 minutes in first-team games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth, for the forward to be assigned the No.77 squad number and to have the name "Gabriel JR" on his shirt.

items.text:
🧠 We Need Smart People Who Give a Shit
Something I learned a long time ago, something that's been proven to me time and again, is that the world is held together by smart people who give a shit. This truth always comes into stark focus when I learn how a complex system functions—or, rather, how it barely functions.
When I worked at Stripe I learned a lot about various banking and money movement systems, and it's terrifying how flawed and fragile these systems are. ACH is a great example. It's a complex system we rely on every day that is just barely good enough to function. It's old, riddled with flaws, and encumbered with legacy baggage. And yet, despite all of those problems, ACH usually works great and is generally considered to be safe, cheap, and reliable.
The reason there's a mismatch between the technical reality of the ACH system and how it functions in practice is due to a single factor: smart people who give a shit. Every problem with ACH is fixed, patched, bypassed, overridden, routed around, or manually handled by people who have two things:
- Intimate knowledge of the system
- The drive and determination to force the system to work
Those two things feed into each other. You have to care about a complex system to dive deep enough to learn how it works, and when you know a lot about how a complex system works you care more about it, especially if the system is important or critical infrastructure.
Now, you can replace "ACH" above with a myriad of other complex systems—everything from huge infrastructure to nice-to-have apps—and everything I said remains true, both about the systems themselves and the people who keep them running. The world runs on these systems, and they depend on smart people who give a shit. Take those people away, and the systems collapse.
And collapse is what we're starting to see. Some recent examples of various failures from just this past week or so: Microsoft 365, Air Traffic Control, United Airlines' systems, the NSA's network, many major banks, Apple's systems, and more. We're told these failures and problems are not related. They're not the result of a cyberattack. They're not the fault of generative AI.
I guess that depends on how you look at it.
I don't have inside information about what's going on, but my experience dealing with complex systems tells me there's a common through line to all of these disruptions: there aren't enough smart people who give a shit.
So where did they go?
Capitalism has never been particularly kind to smart people who give a shit (or people in general... but I digress). Capitalism does, however begrudgingly, recognize that smart people who give a shit are required to build and maintain complex systems that serve capitalist goals. Thus, those people have been accommodated and incorporated into the system by virtue of their necessity and, in many cases, their rarity.
Now, though, generative AI is here. To the people running the show—leadership and management—it seems like they can get the same or better value (and even more output!) from a machine. The machine is cheaper, works longer, doesn't take sick days or vacations, doesn't ask for any benefits, and never pushes back against a bad idea.
People who don't do the actual work—the people who aren't in the trenches—have a hard time telling the difference between a flawed system held aloft by the drive and determination of smart people who give a shit and slop provided by generative AI. To them it's all just output: words you can read, code that runs, and pixels that look nice to their eye. It's all the same to them, so why does it matter where it comes from?
It matters because generative AI isn't smart, and it doesn't give a shit. What seems like intelligence is an illusion propped up by a massive amount of data strip-mined from the commons with weights that nudge the output toward a generally desirable shape. What seems like care, concern, and attention is just generative AI doing what it's designed to do: telling you what you want to hear. The math and logic that power LLMs are as cold, unfeeling, and indifferent as the laws of physics.
Smart people who give a shit notice things. They connect dots. They notice when things don't feel right. They know when something is about to go off the rails, and they know how to get things back on track. They know how to handle edge cases. They know how to manually handle a unique situation. They know what the right thing to do is, and they know when they need to put in extra effort or time to make something happen. Generative AI falls far short in these areas, but this is the glue that holds complex systems together. More prompting and more output isn't a substitute for this.
It's hard for capitalist leadership to internalize any of that, though. It would be such a relief for them, such a burden lifted, to replace all those smart people who give a shit with generative AI. It would be so much easier to win at capitalism if generative AI lived up to the hype, and there's so much pressure for leadership and management to believe that the hype is real.
Thus, a lot of the smart people who give a shit have been laid off, and the ones that remain are hollowed out. Telling people to stop doing the job they signed up for in favor of babysitting LLMs so they can do that job instead is a great way to make people less smart about the system they used to work on and give less of a shit about it. Every prompt moves them one step further away from the system they used to know inside and out. Every generated output that becomes part of the system means those people understand less about how the system actually works. Those people are robbed of the things that make them smart (the struggle of building and learning) and the things that made them gave a shit (a sense of ownership and close connection with the system).
We've moved from a world dependent on complex and fragile systems held together by smart people who give a shit to a world of complex an

items.text:
Security advisories: multiple vulnerabilities in Regexp and String case conversion
Posted by mame on 18 Nov 2026
Seven vulnerabilities have been discovered in Ruby’s regular expression engine and in the case conversion of strings. We are aware of PoCs that prove some of them can be used to trigger remote code execution. We have released Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 to fix them. We strongly recommend upgrading.
CVE identifiers have been requested for these vulnerabilities but have not been assigned yet, so this advisory refers to them by their GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA) identifiers.
GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5: Heap buffer overflow in case conversion of strings
Ruby has a one-byte heap-based buffer overflow in the case conversion of strings. Changing the case of a crafted string may allow remote code execution. We are aware of PoCs that prove this flaw can be used to trigger RCE in some scenarios.
GHSA-7x2q-68qv-6p8x: Double free in regular expression compilation
Ruby has a double free in its regular expression engine. Compiling a crafted regular expression pattern may allow remote code execution in applications that compile attacker-controlled patterns. We are aware of PoCs that prove this flaw can be used to trigger RCE in some scenarios.
GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px: Integer overflow in case conversion of strings
Ruby has an integer overflow in the case conversion of strings, which causes a heap-based buffer overflow. Changing the case of a crafted string may allow remote code execution. We are aware of PoCs that prove this flaw can be used to trigger RCE in some scenarios.
GHSA-wpqw-5qxg-m68r: Out-of-bounds read in case-insensitive regular expression matching
Ruby has an out-of-bounds read in its regular expression engine. Matching against a crafted regular expression pattern may allow remote code execution in applications that use attacker-controlled patterns. We are aware of PoCs that prove this flaw can lead to memory corruption in an attacker-controlled way.
GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w: Heap buffer overflow in regular expression compilation
Ruby has an integer overflow in its regular expression engine, which causes a heap-based buffer overflow. Compiling a crafted regular expression pattern may allow remote code execution in applications that compile attacker-controlled patterns. We are aware of PoCs that prove this flaw can be used to trigger RCE in some scenarios.
GHSA-7whj-cfh7-xgm4: Heap buffer overflow in Regexp#to_s
Ruby has a heap-based buffer overflow in Regexp#to_s. Converting a crafted regular expression to a string may allow information disclosure or remote code execution in applications that compile attacker-controlled patterns. We are aware of PoCs that prove this flaw can be used to trigger RCE in some scenarios.
GHSA-pvgc-g7gj-pv6h: Out-of-bounds read in case-insensitive backreference matching
Ruby has an out-of-bounds read in its regular expression engine. Matching a crafted string may disclose memory contents or crash the process.
Affected versions
- Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier
- Ruby 3.4.0 through 3.4.12
- Ruby 4.0.0 through 4.0.9
Recommended action
We strongly recommend upgrading to Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14.
Ruby 3.3 is in the security maintenance phase. Ruby 3.2 and earlier have reached their end of life and will not receive these fixes.

items.title: Amidst fears of AI-cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’
items.summary: During his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella lamented the fact that a lot of America’s software systems — including those governing everyday hardware and transportation systems — suffer from unfixable software vulnerabilities that, in the age
items.text:
During his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella lamented the fact that a lot of America’s software systems — including those governing everyday hardware and transportation systems — suffer from unfixable software vulnerabilities that, in the age of AI-aided cyberattacks, are just waiting to be exploited.
“Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable,” Nadella said. “I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet.”
In other words: The smartification of the economy, in which much of the world’s “dumb” devices were hooked up to the internet, is now causing tremendous headaches.
The conversation took place against the backdrop of a wave of recent large-scale outages — including one involving Microsoft Outlook. Others have involved the NSA, the FFA, and Apple. Concerns have swirled that these outages are the result of cyberattacks, although officials have denied those claims. Still, the reality of AI-aided cyberattacks is spurring companies to find new strategies for vulnerability discovery and remediation.
Nadella touched briefly on the recent Outlook situation, noting that the global inconvenience was the result of a “latent bug” that led to a “perfect storm.”
“We put out an incident response, and we’re going to obviously take all of the learnings, both upstream architectural, as well as operational, and fix that,” he added.
“Somebody was telling me about sort of even the transportation systems and the amount of stuff that’s discoverable but with unpatchable firmware,” Nadella also added, on the topic of vulnerable systems. “So we’ll have to really modernize for sure…and then we will have to assess what the threat vector looks like, what our own ability to both detect and then defend in real time looks like.”
Nadella made a broader point, as well, which is that the process of patching software vulnerabilities has escalated to match the speed of potential exploitation, but that this has caused more problems.
“We now have a very powerful tool that finds vulnerabilities,” he said. However, companies used to have more time to test those patches, understand a situation, and deploy them, he said. At the same time, AI has made sophisticated cyberattacks much easier to enact.
“The patch [now] needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild, right? So that’s going to create instability.”

items.text:
Michael van Gerwen targets 'A-game' for James Wade meeting in last-16 clash of Grand Slam of Darts
Michael van Gerwen on his second-round opponent: "James Wade is playing some fantastic darts; he's probably in some of the best form of his life"; pair's meeting a rematch of 2016 final which MVG won; watch the Grand Slam of Darts on Sky Sports Main Event at 7pm, Thursday
Wednesday 18 November 2026 23:45, UK
Michael van Gerwen believes James Wade is "in some of the best form of his life" and says he'll need to bring his "A-game" in order to win their second-round meeting at the Grand Slam of Darts.
Their clash on Thursday night - live on Sky Sports+ and Main Event from 7pm - is a rematch of the 2016 final, in which Van Gerwen claimed the second of his three consecutive titles.
But it's Wade, a three-time runner-up at the event, who is the form player of the pair leading into the last 16 matchup, having dropped only one leg across his two group-stage wins.
Van Gerwen, contrastingly, saw both his wins over Henry Coates and Jeffrey de Graaf come down to last-leg deciders. He averaged 100 against Coates, but that dropped to 90 against De Graaf, a match in which he missed seven match darts.
- Littler stunned by Wattimena at Grand Slam of Darts
- Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results
- Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW
"It wasn't a good game at all," Van Gerwen, seeded 10th at the tournament, told Sky Sports after his victory over De Graaf.
"Sometimes you're not doing what you want to do. That's frustrating, because I know I'm capable of doing a lot more.
"What can I say? I am through to the next round - that's all history now - and it's onto the next one."
The former world No 1 added: "James Wade is playing some fantastic darts, you can't deny that. He's probably in some of the best form of his life.
"I need to make sure I play my A-game if I'm going to beat him - simple as that."
Wade has been in sensational form across 2026, making it to the final of the UK Open, winning the Australian Masters, Flanders Darts Trophy, and the opening Players Championship event back in February.
He knows that, with his form at the minute, he has the game to beat anyone, especially if the contest is a bit of a grudge match.
"I think I am way better than the top 10 but I have had to bumble along," said the seventh seed, who has averaged over 100 in both of his Grand Slam group stage wins against Cam Crabtree (5-1) and Ricky Evans (5-0).
"I think if I was probably a little bit more consistent, I would be better than I am.
"But talk is cheap and all that rubbish. I think I am good enough to beat anyone at the moment, because I like a scrap and no darts player wants to have a scrap.
"Most of them just want to have a little gallivant along the meadows and stuff like that, but I am quite happy to take them to a place where most of the younger players don't want to go and that is when I win games."
Luke Humphries, the 2023 Grand Slam champion, is also in action on Thursday night, against Tom Sykes, while Gian van Veen faces Martin Schindler and Nathan Aspinall takes on Gabriel Clemens.
Mardle: I don't get Van Gerwen at the moment
Sky Sports' Wayne Mardle:
"There has been so much made of James Wade's form. He is playing great.
"I don't really get Michael van Gerwen at the moment. A couple of weeks ago he was playing in a Pro Tour event and was averaging 114, 115. He also looked great in his opening group game here, but then looked really edgy in his second.
"Having said that, normally with Michael, the longer the format the less edgy he looks. I'm not saying he'll beat James, but I don't buy into this narrative that Michael is off. He's just not as consistent as he used to be.
"He portrays a lack of confidence at times with what he says, which I don't like.
"I believe he is capable of growing into a game. His confidence grows after a couple of decent legs.
"But if James Wade gets on top of him, I don't like Van Gerwen's chances from there."

Today Anthropic, PBC priced its initial public offering of its Class A common stock at $83.00 per share. The offering consists of 980,000,000 shares of Class A common stock, 956,351,354 of which are being sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 of which are being sold by certain selling stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders.
The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026 under the symbol “ANT.” The offering is expected to close on November 20, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. In addition, Anthropic has granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 147,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock.
A registration statement relating to these securities was declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 18, 2026. The offering is being made only by means of a prospectus. items.title: Elon Musk says ousting Jensen Huang is like ‘kicking Michael Jordan off your team’
items.summary: Elon Musk has already been vocal about his disapproval of the Nvidia board’s decision to oust its founder and CEO Jensen Huang after a series of extramarital affairs were made public, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who is suspected of feeding sensitive information back to Beijing. At The
items.text:
Elon Musk has already been vocal about his disapproval of the Nvidia board’s decision to oust its founder and CEO Jensen Huang after a series of extramarital affairs were made public, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who is suspected of feeding sensitive information back to Beijing. At The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk elaborated on his thoughts about Nvidia’s leadership change.
“Jensen is an old friend of mine,” Musk said. “I would call Jensen, you know, Michael Jordan at his peak level, in terms of what he means to a team.”
On X, the social media platform he owns, Musk even said he would hire Huang.
“He’s one of the most talented entrepreneur-CEOs in history,” Musk said when asked about his X post. “Who wouldn’t want to hire Jensen?”
Musk also signed a petition, alongside over 200,000 other people, urging Nvidia to reinstate its former CEO. Nvidia’s board, however, confirmed it is not planning to bring Huang back.
“[It] doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me…,” Musk said of that decision. “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen.”
He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades,” Musk added. “He understands technology incredibly well. His team loves him… and many of them are there because of him, and have higher offers to go elsewhere, and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen.”
Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey also said that he thinks Nvidia is making the wrong decision by not reinstating Huang.
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said earlier in the day at the DealBook event. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”
Musk also did not express concern over what Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could mean for U.S. national security.
“I don’t think he’s disloyal to the United States,” Musk said. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders.”
Other peers in the industry, like Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, reaffirmed their faith in Nvidia to move forward without its founder and CEO of 33 years at the helm.
“It’s the Nvidia board’s decision, but I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella said at DealBook. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”

items.title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
items.summary: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without a
items.text:
New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.”
The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
Google is trying to force Gemini on schools, and they’re not thrilled.
Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times, New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”
In a statement to The Verge, Google spokesperson Laura Breen said, “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn. To improve Search for the classroom, we’re starting to pilot Guided Learning capabilities in Search this month to walk students step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers. Next year, we’re also updating our approach to controls for schools to address feedback we’ve heard from educators, so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable. We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers.”
Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills, and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests. There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age. But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

items.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remains confident in Nvidia after Huang’s exit
items.summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella weighed in on former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unexpected departure amid a series of shocking controversies.
“It’s all sort of pretty tragic in the sense of, you know, Jensen is somebody I’ve known for a long time. I’ve admired what he’s done, and at this point, I kind of
items.text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella weighed in on former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unexpected departure amid a series of shocking controversies.
“It’s all sort of pretty tragic in the sense of, you know, Jensen is somebody I’ve known for a long time. I’ve admired what he’s done, and at this point, I kind of want to give him space to figure this out,” Nadella said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.
Huang stepped down last week from his CEO role, which he has held for 33 years. Huang’s leadership has been central to Nvidia’s ascent to one of the world’s most valuable companies, but his judgment was questioned after it was reported that he had an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy feeding information back to Beijing. It was also revealed that Huang was having affairs with two Nvidia employees, including one who was a direct report.
While the world waits to see what the long-term economic impacts of Huang’s departure might be, Nadella says he still has confidence in Nvidia, which is a close partner of Microsoft.
“I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella added. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO at Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I’m in touch with the same set of people I was in touch with before [Huang left], so I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”
Microsoft is not unlike Nvidia in that its founder Bill Gates inhabited a larger-than-life persona as CEO.
“Founders are unbelievable in the sense that they create something from nothing, so that is pretty magical… They’re singular, but they’re not gods, right?” Nadella said. “I used to say to Bill [Gates]… Founders also die, and so at some point, a company, if it needs to succeed, it has to have someone take over.”

items.title: Wattimena wins hearts with win vs Littler: 'Beat him, the crowd loves you'
items.summary:
Jermaine Wattimena wins Wolverhampton hearts with victory over Luke Littler: 'You beat him, the crowd loves you'
Jermaine Wattimena put in a stunning performance to come up with a 10-8 win and dump Luke Littler out of the Grand Slam in the second round; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolve
items.text:
Jermaine Wattimena wins Wolverhampton hearts with victory over Luke Littler: 'You beat him, the crowd loves you'
Jermaine Wattimena put in a stunning performance to come up with a 10-8 win and dump Luke Littler out of the Grand Slam in the second round; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22
Wednesday 18 November 2026 23:16, UK
Jermaine Wattimena was visibly emotional following his massive 10-8 win over Luke Littler in the last 16 at the Grand Slam of Darts, taking in the moment as the Wolverhampton crowd sang his name.
An English crowd chanting so heartily for a Dutch player is somewhat of a rarity, especially when they are taking on an Englishman, but it was the sensational manner of his victory over the world No 1 and back-to-back Grand Slam champion that won them over.
Littler was aiming for a Grand Slam three-peat after his wins in 2024 and 2025 but with the Dutchman prevailing, it is still only Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen who have achieved such a feat.
Wattimena led 3-2 before running away to get 7-2 up against Littler. He then held on as Littler fought back to 9-8 and pinned 77 on tops for what is now the biggest win of his career.
It was made all the sweeter given the fact Wattimena has felt the pain of a massive Littler comeback before. He was 7-2 up against 'The Nuke' at the Matchplay in 2025 before eventually being beaten.
"Brilliant. One word needed, brilliant," Wattimena said.
"To be honest, I was thinking about the Matchplay in 2025 when I was 7-2 up. Now I am feeling that again but then the 77 goes in.
"I beat Luke Humphries in the European Championship and this is a bigger win than Luke Humphries then.
"I think you have seen me playing and I played with a lot of confidence. I was really concentrating in the match and I think I can go further than this.
"To be honest, I always play well against Luke Littler but to finally beat him on stage, I am really happy with that.
"I think my scoring power was better than his scoring power. He had to do it against me as well, but I don't think he did.
"They sang my name and I was emotional. That was really brilliant.
"If you beat Luke Littler then the crowd loves you."
Wattimena beat Littler back in August on the way to picking up a Players Championship title.
It was that win that reinforced for Wattimena that he could do the same again on the TV stage.
"I think (that win) gave me some confidence and then you know that he is not unbeatable as well. He is a human, he is not a robot," he added.
"He is a good player, he's an amazing player, everyone knows it but I am more than happy to beat him here at the Grand Slam.
"He got me here two years ago with a high score, but now I got one back.
"When you go to a tournament, you have to think that you can win the title, to be honest.
"You play tournaments to win something. It is a long way to go, but I am here for a win.
"I have got a day off tomorrow, so I have got nothing to do. I will be jumping in the jacuzzi, jumping in the swimming pool, so I'm all relaxed tomorrow."

items.title: Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web
items.summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella predicts that the rise of AI agents is going to reshape the economics of the internet, impacting the business models of the companies that rely on advertising and what he referred to as “human web” traffic.
Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the
items.text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella predicts that the rise of AI agents is going to reshape the economics of the internet, impacting the business models of the companies that rely on advertising and what he referred to as “human web” traffic.
Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the tech executive argued that the shift to an agentic web could change which companies pay others for traffic and for transactions, similar to how the transition from web portals like Yahoo to search engines like Google did years ago.
“The current aggregators who have a business model which was for the human web will get, in some sense, reshuffled,” said Nadella. “And if you were monetizing ads because of the eyeballs, you now have to probably get down to essentially maybe CPC [cost-per-click] wins; maybe it’s more transactional,” he continued. “And so if you don’t accept the agent, somebody else will.”
The discussion turned to Amazon and its decision to block AI agents from accessing its retail website, preventing them from browsing its catalog and making purchases on behalf of their users. Nadella suggested that companies trying to protect their existing business models could lose out to others that are more willing to embrace the AI agents. For instance, if Amazon continues blocking agents, another shopping platform such as Shopify, could allow them, and gain an advantage.
“I think this is going to be interesting,” he said, speaking to the changing models. “It’s the same thing that’s happening in other categories, right? Which is, if you’re in love with a particular business model, you have to kind of scramble,” he said.

items.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
items.summary: In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, hi
items.text:
In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.
Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.
In the six years after being crowned kings of Europe, United turned to Wilf McGuinness, Busby stepped in temporarily to keep them up, then Frank O’Farrell was appointed before they landed on Tommy Docherty, who experienced the ignominy of taking them down.
In the past eight years, United have sacked José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjær, Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and now Michael Carrick.
How did the United of 1974 go down? Most outsiders believed they were too big to fail. Inside the club, though, they sensed the direction of travel. After a heavy defeat at Crystal Palace in December 1972, Busby offered Docherty the job in the Selhurst Park boardroom. “There’s a lot of trouble in the camp,” Busby said. Docherty was doing well as Scotland manager and took a few days to mull it over, but decided he couldn’t turn down the opportunity.
When Busby called him on the Sunday evening, he accepted. “You know it won’t be easy?” Busby said. “It’ll be like turning an oil tanker round, only bigger.” He added: “You might find yourself having to take a step back in order to take a leap forward.” Docherty wrote in his autobiography, The Doc, that at the time he never believed Busby was alluding to relegation.
Docherty was given free rein for a rebuild. The day after his appointment, he signed George Graham from Arsenal for £120,000, a sizeable fee at the time. Alex Forsyth followed from Partick for £100,000 and Docherty pulled off a coup when he persuaded Lou Macari to join bottom-of-the-table United instead of Liverpool for £200,000.
The giants of the previous era were moved on. In February, Bobby Charlton told him that, at 37, it would be his last season. Other big names wanted to stay, but Docherty felt a reset was needed. “The Manchester United team that had won the European Cup in 1968 was without a doubt a great team, but many members of that side had been allowed to grow old together,” he wrote.
“I knew what I had decided would prove very unpopular with many people but it had to be done. I set out my stall to end the United careers of among others Denis Law, Tony Dunne, Pat Crerand and David Sadler.”
George Best, who had retired once but returned under Docherty, played his last game on New Year’s Day 1974 after repeatedly turning up late. The most controversial departure was Law, who was allowed to join Manchester City.
Having taken over with United bottom, Docherty kept them up in his first season and was emboldened to continue his clearout. Thirteen players were released that summer. But halfway through the following season they were facing relegation again and a lack of goals cost them. At one stage, the joint-top scorer was Alex Stepney, with two penalties. He was the goalkeeper.
Relegation was confirmed on the penultimate day as they lost to City, a defeat made all the more painful by Law back-heeling the late winner. Docherty was interviewed on the Old Trafford pitch and asked, in a scene replayed in TNT Sports’ Too Good To Go Down, whether the club would drift into obscurity. “No, there’s no danger,” he said. “We could wash the jerseys here and hang them out to dry and you’d get 15,000 people standing watching them do so.”
Despite the bravado, Docherty was expecting the sack when he met Busby a few days later. Instead, Busby handed him a case of champagne, reminded him of the oil tanker and told him to set to work getting them back up.
Docherty’s prediction proved right: the brand was far bigger than the division they played in. In the Second Division, Old Trafford averaged crowds of more than 47,000 – the biggest in the country – and their away support descended on towns and cities and routinely outnumbered the home contingent.
Docherty bought young and hungry, targeting players with a point to prove, including Steve Coppell from Tranmere, Stuart Pearson from Hull and Jim Holton from Shrewsbury. The direct, attacking football synonymous with United returned and the Scot shaped a fearless 4-2-4 formation.
Crowds grew after they came straight back up and for a while United were on course to become the fifth side to win the First Division after promotion, but finished third and also reached the FA Cup final, losing 1-0 to Southampton. That shows the stark differences between then and now.
The gap between the first and second tiers was narrower. United did not lose a gargantuan broadcast deal when they went down. They were not saddled with debt by their owners. Their wage bill was not tied to Champions League qualification. Players were not on long contracts and were easier to buy and sell. There were no disruptive agents. Fans were more patient.
If lessons of the 1970s are not heeded soon, the fallout could be infinitely more painful.

items.text:
LLM assisted reverse engineering
I have been hacking both hardware and software for 2 decades. Previously manually. But in 2026 with the help of AIs the proccess is greatly sped up. Below I will describe my proccess briefly or how I do it.
Set Up
Tools which I mostly use are these:
Process
What I basically do nowadays is just point the agent at the binary to be analysed and use my set of dedicated agent skills. Rest usually takes care of itself. But putting the skills besides, the flow is basically this.
- Find binary type, platform, build etc - based on this using appropriate decompiler (note - current AIs do fairly well with just disassembly . ie pure x86 or ARM instructions).
- Command agent to document all findings along the way to MD files. This serves several purposes. They become notes for your own understanding. They help the agent not lose the track after compaction / handoff to different agent. And last but not least, it helps the agent work more effectively, not get lost in circles etc. More about this later.
- Ask the agent to analyse basic structure. Main functions, main branching, imported functions etc of given binary. By binary I mean whatever. Desktop executable, website or firmware image.
Once I have this basic overview I can usually proceed any way I need to do modifications to the original binary or build mods or just help me understand it better.
On some occasions some things are not easily resolvable by simple disassembly or decompilation. In those cases you can do:
- Let the agent debug given binary and set breakpoints on specific parts to help it figure out given inner workings.
- Use logging. Either by somehow enabling it in the original binary or by making a probe (and this can mean many things) that injects to the original binary and records you via logs (to file) whatever is needed to resolve given feature.
- Give agent outside access - ie computer use for desktop apps, or api controllable emulator for running and controlling given firmware.
- Ask agent to try different approach. But you must be specific. Ie when it gets stuck in disasembly by following xrefs, ask it to try to follow strings in the binary instead.
- Read the entire LLM conversation and thinking. Current LLMs are smart but they still sometimes get to a narrow approach. By reading the traces you can often instinctively figure the agent it going into a blind path and give it suggestion as to how it might be approached better. That however skill of your own to have.
SKILLS
Here are some of my major skills I use frequently.
Matt Pottock - Grill me
It gives you several questions when your input might be valuable. I usually use it with this prompt:
Ghidra / other RE tooling skill
It helps a ton to have a skill where your specific reverse engineering tooling is described. Ie to use radare2 or kuna. Or description of how to use the MCP Ghidra bridge and for what. Without such a skill, agents often give up too quickly getting lost, not knowing how to do the actual disassembly / decompilation.
Hypothesis debugging
That is also my own skill. Its related to how I wrote earlier how important it is to make the agent document everything into MD files. This skill forces agent who is getting stuck to follow this loop:
- Make a hypothesis of why / how something works. Write it down into CSV table of hypotheses, saved on disc.
- Design experiment (probe, logging, ...) which will definitively prove or disprove this hypothesis.
- Record the result.
- Repeat.
This is variation of scientific method and it significantly helps agents when they are getting stuck on some problem. Stops it going in circles. By forcing it to do definitive experiments. No endless guessing and trying random things. This one is crucial in my opinion. I made it public too, so other can benefit from it.
Implementation of hacks and probes
For implementing anything I basically go for 2 toolings.
- Python but with UV tooling. UV tooling allows to make custom envs super quickly and portably. Also allows to make single-file, inline dependencies scripts. Python is great for prototyping or quickly making probes or even decompilation helpers.
- Rust for actual implementation of given hack. Whenever it is possible I am using rust for this. It has many reasons but he two main are:
- it is very elegant language for me personally to work with and
- it provides brutally good feedback loops to the agent when it iterates - the compiler is very strict and points the agent immediately to any possible memory or syntax issues he might be heading to.
Of course rust has also its downsides, like slower compile times, but overal its mature language with plethora of build targets (I have implemented in it webs, desktop apps, hacks / trainers but even firmwares for various embedded languages).
My hacking successes
With the AI assisted reverse engineering I was able to achieve such crazy reverse engineering succeses, in the last 6 months, which would take me years each on its own, if done by hands.
- Reverse engineered and hacked Alphasmart NEO typewriting device
- Completely mapped communication protocols of many devices like EmWave biofeedback device or both my Sony Alpha mirrorless cameras. Allowing me to make custom desktop and mobile apps for file transfer, wireless control and more. I even managed to make this way a wireless webcam from my A7III mirrorless camera.
- Hacked into and developed custom firmwares for musical synthesizers:
  - Arturia MiniFreak
  - Teenage Engineering OP-Z
  - Akai MPC Sample
- Made custom firmware for Xteink X4 ebook reader
- Fixed driver for old HP printer for MacOs
- Cracked tons of license-locked abandonware softwares from my youth
- Developed custom lightweight Evernote client
- And many more
Sometimes its a thin boundary between reverse engineering and software development. Sometimes you just decipher the proprietary save file format of the ugly paid app and then move into the clean software development phase of building your new,

items.title: Anthropic reportedly prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range
items.summary: Anthropic has reportedly priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in
items.text:
Anthropic has reportedly priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in the industry.
At the IPO price, Anthropic is reportedly valued at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, a significant increase from the $965 billion the company reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private market backers set to round, but below the $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for several months ago.
Anthropic will begin its life as a public company on Thursday, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” A strong first day of trading would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption, despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks.
The company’s performance is expected to set expectations for private AI companies, including Anthropic’s main rival OpenAI, which was last reportedly valued at $1.25 billion but has yet to announce plans for an IPO.
Although none of Anthropic’s venture capital investors holds more than a 5% stake in the company, the IPO is a massive windfall for its numerous backers. Investors that own approximately 1% of the company reportedly include Sequoia and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC also holds about a 1% stake in the company, according to a person familiar with the matter. Other backers set to make billions are Iconiq, Menlo Ventures, Coatue, and Sound Ventures, a firm launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, and Spark Ventures, the only VC firm known to hold a board seat at the company.
Some of the company’s existing investors, namely Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel, and Altimeter Capital Management, are so enthusiastic about Anthropic’s future that they were reportedly planning to buy billions of dollars’ worth of company’s shares in the IPO.
Yet the investors’ holdings in Anthropic pale in comparison to those of the Claude maker’s strategic partners, Amazon, which owns nearly 15% of the company, and Google, which holds almost 14%. A group of major tech companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners, have also agreed to purchase $26 billion worth of non-voting shares through a private placement alongside the IPO.
The company’s seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, each sold nearly 3.4 million shares in the IPO, according to the S-1 filing, bringing in about $282 million for each.

items.title: Veerle Buurman scrambles late WCL winner to push blunt Chelsea past PSG
items.summary:
Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.
Buurman had stolen the show
items.text:
Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.
Buurman had stolen the show in Chelsea’s defeat of Manchester City at the weekend, coming on 12 minutes in and nullifying Khadija Shaw’s threat to be named player of the match and she was the hero under the lights with Chelsea doing everything but score prior to her goal.
Sonia Bompastor’s side had been frustrated by Häcken last week, held to a 0-0 draw by the Swedish side and falling out of the top four automatic progression places. There was a desire to put things right at AFC Wimbledon’s stadium and they did just that, albeit in not the prettiest of encounters.
PSG had suffered a 2-1 home defeat to Bayern Munich after three draws and one win in the competition ahead of their trip to London. Denied a point late on, they remain 10th and dangerously close to slipping out of a place in the playoffs.
Chelsea had been thrillingly gutsy and diligent in their 1-0 win over Manchester City on Saturday and against PSG they were similarly solid at the back, but they lacked spark in attack. Ellie Carpenter became the focal point of their forward play from the right, with the striker Melvine Malard injured in the game against City.
Malard was one of three changes to Bompastor’s lineup for the visit of the Première Ligue side, having joined an injury list which includes Lauren James, Naomi Girma and Manaka Matsukubo, with Aggie Beever-Jones leading the line in her place while Nathalie Björn and Buurman replaced Lucy Bronze and Kadeisha Buchanan.
Meanwhile, Paulo César also made three changes, travelling to south-west London without PSG’s injured captain, Sakina Karchaoui, and forward Romée Leuchter.
Nullifying the threat of Carpenter blunted Chelsea, and despite their dominance of the ball, amassing 64% possession in the first half, Chelsea struggled to carve a way through the French side’s backline. They had seven attempts on goal to PSG’s six at the break, despite 33 attacks to 10.
Chelsea have historically performed well against PSG, winning three of their four Champions League meetings prior to this penultimate fixture of their league phase campaign. In the 2018-19 quarter-finals they earned a 2-0 home win and, after a 2-1 away defeat, progressed to the semi-finals; in the 2022-23 season they won both group meetings with an overall score of 4-0. The teams that met in those previous encounters look very different today, but there is a lot of familiarity between the WSL leaders and PSG, with Bompastor and her assistant manager Camille Abily having played and coached against them many times while at OL Lyonnes. They also both spent a season on loan from different American clubs in the French capital.
The visiting team’s first attempt on target arrived after the break, with Merveille Kanjinga forcing a near-post save from Hannah Hampton. While Chelsea still dominated, PSG had more forays forward in the second half.
Erin Cuthbert, Maika Hamano and Lucy Bronze arrived at the hour mark as the home team sought to deal the killer blow their dominance required. It increasingly felt like it would take something special to break the deadlock, akin to the sublime effort that Sandy Baltimore had delivered against City.
Beever-Jones was replaced by Sjoeke Nüsken late on and the German instantly made a difference, forcing a sublime save from Katarzyna Kiedrzynek. The breakthrough came from the resulting corner, and it was far less sublime than Saturday’s effort, Buurman somehow squeezing the ball in at the near post after PSG failed to clear Cuthbert’s ball in.
It was the bit of luck Chelsea needed and they look increasingly formidable.
